ITQAN:v2p415/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p415/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p415/r3.claim: Dhikr can refer to the five daily prayers.
ITQAN:v2p415/r3.anchor: والصلوات الخمس ﴿ فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله ﴾

STUDYQURAN:2:239/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r1.claim: The fear may arise during battle or persecution.
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r1.anchor: One can be fearful when in battle or under persecution

STUDYQURAN:2:239/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r2.claim: In fear, including open warfare, prayer may be performed on foot or mounted, facing the qiblah or in another direction.
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r2.anchor: in cases of fear, such as during open warfare, one can pray while riding or walking, whether it is in the direction of the qiblah (facing the Kaʿbah) or not

STUDYQURAN:2:239/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r3.claim: Instead of bowing and prostrating, a person may nod and move the head lightly to correspond with the prayer motions.
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r3.anchor: One can, rather than bow and prostrate, nod and lightly move one’s head in a manner corresponding to the motions of the prayer

STUDYQURAN:2:239/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r4.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r4.claim: Some allow the prayer to be shortened to a single cycle instead of two, three, or four.
STUDYQURAN:2:239/r4.anchor: according to some, one can shorten one’s prayers down to one cycle of prayer, rather than two, three, or four (IK)

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r1.claim: When people fear an enemy may harm them, they may perform the prayer on foot or mounted during battle; this substitutes for standing in full, composed prayer.
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r1.anchor: أن تصلوا قياما على أرجلكم بالأرض، قانتين لله، فصلوا رجالا مشاة على أرجلكم، وأنتم في حربكم،

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r2.claim: The accusative رجالا is licensed by an omitted conditional answer: if you fear praying standing on the ground, then pray on foot; Arabic may coordinate the answer with the condition.
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r2.anchor: بمعنى: إن خفتم أن تصلوا قياما بالأرض فصلوا رجالا

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r3.claim: رجالا is the plural of راجل or رجل, meaning a person walking on foot.
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r3.anchor: والرجال جمع راجل ورجل. وأما أهل الحجاز فإنهم يقولون لواحد الرجال رجل، مسموع منهم

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r4.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r4.claim: Some Arabs use رجلان for a male pedestrian, رجلى for a female, and رجالى for a mixed or masculine plural; a verse by a man of Banu ʿUqayl illustrates the singular form.

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r5.claim: Two reported noncanonical readings of فرجالا, one with a doubled consonant, are inadmissible because they depart from the widespread inherited reading.
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r5.anchor: وقد حكي عن بعضهم أنه كان يقرأ ذلك: «فإن خفتم فرجالا» مشددة.

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r6.claim: ركبانا is a plural of راكب; other Arabic plurals include ركب، ركبة، ركاب، أركب، and أركوب.
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r6.anchor: وأما الركبان، فجمع راكب، يقال: هو راكب وهو ركبان وركب وركبة وركاب وأركب وأركوب

TAB-FULL:v4p384/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r7.claim: Ibrahim says that during pursuit one prays facing whatever direction one is headed, on foot or mounted, gesturing with prostration lower than bowing, for two rakʿahs.
TAB-FULL:v4p384/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال: سألته عن قوله: {فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: عند المطاردة يصلي حيث كان وجهه،

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r1.claim: Ibrahim describes the prayer during sword fighting as two rakʿahs performed with gestures.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r1.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: " {فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: صلاة الضراب ركعتين يومئ إيماء "

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r2.claim: Ibrahim says one prays two rakʿahs with gestures while facing the direction one happens to be facing.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r2.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قوله: " {فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: يصلي ركعتين حيث كان وجهه يومئ إيماء "

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when horses are pursuing, one prays by gesturing.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r3.anchor: عن سالم، عن سعيد بن جبير، " {فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: إذا طردت الخيل فأومئ إيماء "

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r4.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r4.claim: Saʿid says the prayer is performed with gestures.

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says that in combat one prays mounted or walking, facing any direction and gesturing.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r5.anchor: ثنا هشيم، عن يونس، عن الحسن، " {فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: إذا كان عند القتال صلى راكبا أو ماشيا

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r6.claim: Mujahid says the verse concerns the Prophet’s Companions in battle: pray in any direction, standing or mounted as able, gesturing with the head or speaking with the tongue.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r6.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] أصحاب محمد

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says that when combatants meet, pursue, or are pursued, or a beast pursues them, they pray by two takbirs with gestures in any direction.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: إذا التقوا عند القتال وطلبوا،

TAB-FULL:v4p387/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says during combat or pursuit one prays facing any direction on foot or mounted, gesturing for one rakʿah, or two takbirs if unable.
TAB-FULL:v4p387/r8.anchor: أخبرنا جويبر، عن الضحاك " في قوله: " فرجالا أو ركبانا قال: ذلك عند القتال يصلي حيث كان وجهه

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says a person may pray one rakʿah while walking, being carried by a camel, or riding a galloping horse in any direction.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r1.anchor: عن الفضل بن دلهم، عن الحسن: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: ركعة وأنت تمشي،

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says a foot soldier gestures with the head wherever facing, and a rider gestures likewise from the mount.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r2.anchor: ثنا أسباط، عن السدي: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] أما رجالا: فعلى أرجلكم إذا قاتلتم،

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r3.claim: Qatada says combat fear permits prayer mounted or running, gesturing with the head toward any direction; pray two rakʿahs if able, otherwise one.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r3.anchor: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] الآية. أحل الله لك إذا كنت خائفا عند القتال أن تصلي

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r4.speaker: طاووس
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r4.claim: Tawus says this concession applies during sword fighting.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r4.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: ذاك عند المسايفة "

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r5.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri says when enemies pursue, people may pray two rakʿahs in any direction on foot or mounted with gestures; Qatada says one rakʿah suffices.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r5.anchor: عن معمر، عن الزهري، في قوله: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: إذا طلب الأعداء فقد حل لهم أن يصلوا

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r6.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says that when they fear the enemy, they pray two rakʿahs whether mounted or walking.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r6.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، في قوله: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: كانوا إذا خشوا العدو صلوا ركعتين راكبا كان أو راجلا "

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r7.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r7.claim: Ibrahim says the obligatory prayer in combat may be performed on a mount in any direction, gesturing at each bow and prostration with the latter lower; this applies when swords clash and during pursuit.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r7.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: يصلي الرجل في القتال المكتوبة على دابته،

TAB-FULL:v4p389/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r8.claim: Qatada reiterates that one may pray mounted or walking with gestures, performing two rakʿahs if able and otherwise one.
TAB-FULL:v4p389/r8.anchor: ثنا معاذ بن هشام، قال: ثني أبي، قال: كان قتادة، يقول: " إن استطاع ركعتين وإلا فواحدة يومئ إيماء

TAB-FULL:v4p390/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says a person pursued by an enemy should pray two rakʿahs if able, otherwise one; another report from him simply says one.
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، قال: " في الخائف الذي يطلبه العدو، قال: إن استطاع أن يصلي ركعتين، وإلا صلى ركعة "

TAB-FULL:v4p390/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r2.speaker: الحكم، حماد، قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r2.claim: Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Qatada say the prayer during sword fighting is one rakʿah, with gestures in whichever direction one faces.
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r2.anchor: سألت الحكم، وحمادا، وقتادة، عن صلاة المسايفة، فقالوا: ركعة

TAB-FULL:v4p390/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r3.speaker: ابن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r3.claim: Asked about the prayer of someone fleeing, Ibn Sirin says to pray however one is able.
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r3.anchor: عن أشعث بن سوار، قال: " سألت ابن سيرين، عن صلاة المنهزم، فقال: كيف استطاع "

TAB-FULL:v4p390/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r4.speaker: هرم بن حيان
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r4.claim: During battle, Hurm ibn Hayyan ordered each fighter to make a prostration in whatever direction faced; he also allowed a prostration under the collar or whatever gesture was possible.
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r4.anchor: عن أبي نضرة، عن جابر بن غراب، قال: " كنا نقاتل القوم وعلينا هرم بن حيان، فحضرت الصلاة، فقالوا: الصلاة الصلاة فقال هرم: يسجد الرجل حيث كان وجهه سجدة.

TAB-FULL:v4p390/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r5.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r5.claim: Ata says one may perform the obligatory prayer in any direction while mounted or walking, following the direction the animal takes, with gestures.
TAB-FULL:v4p390/r5.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن أبي سليمان، عن عطاء، في قوله: " {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: تصلي حيث توجهت راكبا وماشيا،

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r1.claim: Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah says the fear prayer is one rakʿah.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: «صلاة الخوف ركعة»

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r2.claim: Ata says that a fearful person prays in whatever condition is possible.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r2.anchor: عن عبد الملك، عن عطاء، في هذه الآية، قال: «إذا كان خائفا صلى على أي حال كان»

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r3.speaker: مالك
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r3.claim: Malik takes رجالا here to mean pedestrians, contrasted with mounted people; he supports this from 22:27, where pilgrims come walking and on every lean camel.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r3.anchor: قال مالك، وسألته عن قول الله: " {فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] قال: راكبا وماشيا، ولو كانت إنما عني بها الناس، لم يأت إلا رجالا وانقطعت الألف إنما هي رجال مشاة.

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r4.claim: The concession covers obligatory prayer while walking or riding in urgent combat against an enemy or combatant, pursuit, a predator, a charging camel, or a flood threatening drowning.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r4.anchor: الخوف الذي للمصلي أن يصلي من أجله المكتوبة ماشيا راجلا، وراكبا جائلا: الخوف على المهمة عند السلة،

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r5.claim: The danger must be likely to kill if the person completes prayer with its ordinary requirements; this is what defines severe fear.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r5.anchor: وإنما قلنا: إن الخوف الذي يجوز للمصلي أن يصلي كذلك هو الذي الأغلب منه الهلاك بإقامة الصلاة بحدودها،

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r6.claim: Because the verse states the concession generally and restricts it only by the described degree of fear, no particular kind of danger is excluded.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r6.anchor: لعموم كتاب الله: {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} [البقرة: 239] ولم يخص الخوف على ذلك على نوع من الأنواع،

TAB-FULL:v4p392/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r7.claim: The Prophet describes the usual fear prayer: the imam leads one contingent for one prostration while another guards; the groups exchange, each completes one prostration, and in greater fear people pray walking or mounted.
TAB-FULL:v4p392/r7.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عمر، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة الخوف: «يقوم الأمير وطائفة من الناس معه، فيسجدون سجدة واحدة، ثم تكون طائفة

TAB-FULL:v4p394/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that in intermingled combat only remembrance with a head gesture is possible; the Prophet distinguished this severe fear from the case where people pray standing or mounted.
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r1.anchor: عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال: «إذا اختلطوا يعني في القتال فإنما هو الذكر، وأشار بالرأس» قال ابن عمر: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فيصلون قياما وركبانا»

TAB-FULL:v4p394/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r2.claim: The Prophetic distinction between ordinary fear prayer and intermingled combat shows that this verse concerns the severe fear described by al-Tabari.
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r2.anchor: ففصل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين حكم صلاة الخوف في غير حال المسايفة، والمطاردة وبين حكم صلاة الخوف في حال شدة الخوف والمسايفة،

TAB-FULL:v4p394/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar describes the ordinary fear prayer: the imam leads one group for a rakʿah as the other guards, then the groups exchange and each completes a rakʿah; if fear is more severe, pray walking or mounted.
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r3.anchor: عن أيوب، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، أنه قال في صلاة الخوف: «يصلى بطائفة من القوم ركعة وطائفة تحرس، ثم ينطلق هؤلاء

TAB-FULL:v4p394/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers retaining the full prayer count prescribed in safety; if a person reduces it in this danger, one rakʿah is still valid.
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r4.anchor: وأما عدد الركعات في تلك الحال من الصلاة، فإني أحب أن لا يقتصر من عددها في حال الأمن،

TAB-FULL:v4p394/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that prayer was prescribed as four rakʿahs at home, two in travel, and one in fear.
TAB-FULL:v4p394/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس، قال: «فرض الله الصلاة على لسان نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحضر أربعا، وفي السفر ركعتين، وفي الخوف ركعة»

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r1.claim: When believers are safe from enemies or other threats that could kill them during prayer, they are reassured and should remember God in prayer and beyond it.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r1.anchor: فإذا أمنتم أيها المؤمنون من عدوكم أن يقدر على قتلكم في حال اشتغالكم بصلاتكم

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r2.claim: Remembering God means thanking, praising, and extolling Him for enabling believers to find the truth from which disbelievers strayed.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r2.anchor: فاذكروا الله في صلاتكم وفي غيرها، بالشكر له، والحمد، والثناء عليه

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r3.claim: God taught believers rulings, lawful and forbidden matters, histories of earlier peoples, future worldly and afterlife events, and other knowledge they previously lacked.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r3.anchor: من أحكامه، وحلاله، وحرامه، وأخبار من قبلكم من الأمم السالفة، والأنباء الحادثة بعدكم

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets becoming safe as leaving the abode of travel and returning to the abode of residence.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r4.anchor: عن ليث، عن مجاهد: " {فإذا أمنتم} [البقرة: 196] قال: خرجتم من دار السفر إلى دار الإقامة "

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says that once safe, people pray as prescribed because fear had granted a concession; he interprets ذكر الله here as prayer.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله} [البقرة: 239] قال: فإذا أمنتم فصلوا الصلاة كما افترض الله عليكم

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r6.claim: Al-Tabari rejects Mujahid’s travel-based reading: everyone agrees that once fear ends, obligatory prayer resumes its full standing, bowing, and prostration form, with only travel shortening allowed.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r6.anchor: لإجماع الجميع على أن الخوف متى زال فواجب على المصلي المكتوبة وإن كان في سفر أداؤها بركوعها وسجودها

TAB-FULL:v4p395/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r7.claim: The passage contrasts prayer during safety with prayer during severe fear, not travel; if settling from travel were intended, the wording would say إقامة, while أمنتم and the context support resuming ordinary prayer.
TAB-FULL:v4p395/r7.anchor: وإنما جرى ذكر الصلاة في حال الأمن وحال شدة الخوف، فعرف الله سبحانه وتعالى عباده صفة الواجب عليهم من الصلاة فيهما، ثم قال: فإذا أمنتم

TABATABAI:2:239#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r10.claim: The conditional clause depends on an omitted condition: preserve prayer when you do not fear; under fear, perform it as far as possible, walking or riding. This is the prayer of fear.
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r10.anchor: عطف الشرط على الجملة السابقة يدل على تقدير شرط محذوف

TABATABAI:2:239#2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r11.claim: Prayer is never dropped: when fear makes normal performance difficult, pray to the extent possible; when safety returns, the ordinary obligation resumes along with remembrance of God.
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r11.anchor: بل إن لم تخافوا شيئا وأمكنت لكم وجبت عليكم

TABATABAI:2:239#2/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r12.claim: The kāf expresses comparison, and the broad phrase what you did not know replaces a narrower reference to emphasize the breadth of God's teaching and favor.
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r12.anchor: من قبيل وضع العام موضع الخاص

TABATABAI:2:239#2/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r13.claim: After safety returns, remember God in a way resembling the prescribed prayer taught for secure conditions, within the broader body of religious rulings He taught.
TABATABAI:2:239#2/r13.anchor: فاذكروا الله ذكرا يماثل ما علمكم من الصلاة المفروضة المكتوبة

TABRISI:2:239/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r1.claim: Rijālan is the plural of rāجل, one who is on foot, standing or walking; rukbān is the plural of rāكب, one who rides or is mounted.
TABRISI:2:239/r1.anchor: الرجال جمع راجل مثل تجار وصحاب وقيام

TABRISI:2:239/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r2.claim: The root of riding means to mount or be above something; rikāb can mean riding camels, and the root extends to striking a body part with one's knee.
TABRISI:2:239/r2.anchor: وكل شيء علا شيئا فقد ركبه والركاب المطي

TABRISI:2:239/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r3.claim: Rijālan is an accusative circumstantial expression with an implied command: pray on foot.
TABRISI:2:239/r3.anchor: رجالا منصوب على الحال تقديره فصلوا رجالا

TABRISI:2:239/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r4.claim: The kāf in kamā is attached to udhkurū, mā is a verbal noun, and mā lam takūnū taʿlamūn is a relative clause serving as the second object of ʿallama.
TABRISI:2:239/r4.anchor: كما علمكم الكاف يتعلق باذكروا وما مصدرية في ما علمكم

TABRISI:2:239/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r5.claim: After establishing the duty to maintain prayer, the passage gives a concession for circumstances of fear.
TABRISI:2:239/r5.anchor: لما قدم سبحانه وجوب المحافطة على الصلاة عقبه بذكر الرخصة عند المخافة

TABRISI:2:239/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r6.claim: Fear here is danger that prevents worshippers from standing in devotion and fulfilling prayer properly.
TABRISI:2:239/r6.anchor: أي إن لم يمكنكم أن تقوموا قانتين موفين الصلاة حقها

TABRISI:2:239/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r7.claim: In fear, pray on foot or walking, or mounted on the backs of animals; this refers to the fear prayer against an enemy.
TABRISI:2:239/r7.anchor: أي فصلوا رجالا على أرجلكم وقيل مشاة

TABRISI:2:239/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r8.claim: The fear prayer consists of two rakʿas in travel and residence, except for the three-rakʿa Maghrib prayer.
TABRISI:2:239/r8.anchor: وصلاة الخوف من العدو ركعتان في السفر والحضر إلا المغرب فإنها ثلاث ركعات

TABRISI:2:239/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r9.speaker: علي
TABRISI:2:239/r9.claim: It is reported that ʿAlī prayed five prayers on the night of al-Harīr by gestures, or, in another report, by takbīr.
TABRISI:2:239/r9.anchor: ويروى أن عليا صلى ليلة الهرير خمس صلوات بالإيماء وقيل بالتكبير

TABRISI:2:239/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r10.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:239/r10.claim: The Prophet prayed by gestures on the day of the Battle of the Trench.
TABRISI:2:239/r10.anchor: وإن النبي صلى يوم الأحزاب إيماء

TABRISI:2:239/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r11.claim: When danger has passed, one explanation is to perform the normal prayer; another is to remember God with praise and thanksgiving.
TABRISI:2:239/r11.anchor: أي فصلوا صلاة الأمن وقيل اذكروا الله بالثناء عليه

TABRISI:2:239/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:239/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:239/r12.claim: God taught them matters of religion as well as other matters they had not known.
TABRISI:2:239/r12.anchor: من أمور دينكم وغير ذلك من أموركم

THALABI:v2p199/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p199/r1.claim: A cited line about Banu Ghudana witnesses the use of rijālan for people walking on foot, contrasted with riding mounts.
THALABI:v2p199/r1.anchor: وبنو غدانة شاخص أبصارهم … يمشون تحت بطونهن رجالا

THALABI:v2p199/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r2.speaker: المفضل
THALABI:v2p199/r2.claim: Rukbānan is the plural of rider; al-Mufaddal says rākib is used only for a camel rider, while a horse, donkey, or mule rider is named for that animal.
THALABI:v2p199/r2.anchor: وهو جمع راكب، قال المفضل: لا يقال راكب إلا لصاحب الجمل،

THALABI:v2p199/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p199/r3.claim: Rijālan and rukbānan are accusative circumstantial expressions: pray walking or riding.
THALABI:v2p199/r3.anchor: ونصبت على الحال، أي فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا.

THALABI:v2p199/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p199/r4.claim: When fear prevents a person from praying with full devotional posture and due observance, prayer while walking or riding suffices.
THALABI:v2p199/r4.anchor: ومعنى الآية: فإن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين الصلاة حقها لخوف

THALABI:v2p199/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r5.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v2p199/r5.claim: Commentators describe prayer amid battle or pursuit facing any direction, mounted or walking, with prostration lower than bowing and gestures; this is severe-fear prayer, discussed again in Surat al-Nisa.
THALABI:v2p199/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: هذا في المسابقة والمطاردة، يصلي حيث يولي وجهه،

THALABI:v2p199/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p199/r6.claim: Permitted causes of such fear include combat or pursuit, a raging beast, an attacking camel, a rushing flood, or any situation in which death is the prevailing expectation.
THALABI:v2p199/r6.anchor: والخوف الذي يجوز للمصلي أن يصلي من أجله راكبا أو

THALABI:v2p199/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p199/r7.claim: Severe-fear prayer is two rakʿahs, though one rakʿah is also valid.
THALABI:v2p199/r7.anchor: وإن صلى صلاة الأمن فله أن يصلي صلاة شدة الخوف وهي ركعتان، فإن صلاها ركعة واحدة جاز

THALABI:v2p199/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p199/r8.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Abbas saying prayer was prescribed as four rakʿahs at home, two while traveling, and one in fear.
THALABI:v2p199/r8.anchor: لما روى مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: فرض الله عز وجل الصلاة على لسان نبيكم

THALABI:v2p199/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v2p199/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when armies clash and people exchange blows, one should say tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, and takbir and remember God; that is the prayer.
THALABI:v2p199/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إذا كنت في القتال، والتقى الزحفان،

THALABI:v2p199/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r10.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v2p199/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri says that if a person cannot even do that, they should still remember God inwardly.
THALABI:v2p199/r10.anchor: قال الزهري: فإن لم يستطع فلا يدع ذكرها في نفسه.

THALABI:v2p199/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p199/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p199/r11.claim: When safe, worshippers should perform the five prayers fully and fulfill their due observances, as God taught them what they did not know.
THALABI:v2p199/r11.anchor: فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله أي فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة لحقوقها كما علمكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r1.claim: The object of fear is omitted because it is evident: the threat is an enemy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r1.anchor: أراد خفتم عدوا فحذف المفعول لإحاطه العلم به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r2.claim: Rijāl is a plural of rājil like tājir/tujjār; a rājil is someone on foot, whether walking or standing, and it has several plural forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r2.anchor: والرجال: جمع راجل، مثل: تاجر وتجار، وصاحب وصحاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r3.claim: Rukbān is the plural of rākib, parallel to fāris/fursān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r3.anchor: والركبان: جمع راكب، مثل: فارس وفرسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r4.claim: If you cannot pray standing and fulfill prayer's full due, pray walking on foot or riding; this suffices.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى الآية: فإن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين للصلاة حقها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r5.claim: Exegetes describe prayer amid sword fighting or pursuit: face the qibla if possible, otherwise not; pronounce the takbir, recite, gesture for bowing and prostration, keep the rakah count, and shorten if traveling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: هذا في المسايفة والمطاردة، يكبر الرجل مستقبل القبلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly says the Prophet prescribed four rakahs at home, two while traveling, and one in fear; the author says this is a school position that is not acted upon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r6.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: فرض الله على لسان نبيكم الصلاة في الحضر أربعا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r7.claim: This is prayer in extreme fear, when a person may pray mounted, gesture, and face any direction; the separate prayer of fear is discussed in Surat al-Nisa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r7.anchor: وهذه صلاة شدة الخوف، وهي التي يجوز للمصلي أن يصلي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r8.claim: Ibn Umar glosses the verse as allowing prayer facing the qibla or not facing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r8.anchor: وقال (¬2) ابن عمر في تفسير هذه الآية: ومستقبلي القبلة وغير مستقبلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r9.claim: Extreme-fear gesture prayer also applies to danger from a predator, flood, charging camel, or other likely peril; a person may gesture and run if the prayer time may be missed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p297#2/r9.anchor: والصلاة بالإيماء في شدة الخوف لا يختص (¬3) بخوف المشركين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r1.claim: When safe, pray the five prayers in full and fulfill their due requirements.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله} فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r2.claim: God's teaching here means that He prescribed the prayers at their appointed times.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p299/r2.anchor: {كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون} يريد: كما افترض عليكم في مواقيتها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r1.claim: If fear prevents prayer with all its due requirements, pray while walking or riding an animal; this applies during pursuit and sword fighting.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r1.anchor: { فإن خفتم فرجالا } أي: إن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا موفين للصلاة حقها فصلوا مشاة على أرجلكم { أو ركبانا }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r2.claim: This emergency prayer applies during pursuit and sword fighting.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r2.anchor: وهذا في المطاردة والمسايفة { فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r3.claim: When safe, perform the five prayers fully with all their requirements.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r3.anchor: { فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله } أي: فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة بحقوقها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r4.claim: God taught them by prescribing prayers at their appointed times.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:239-240/r4.anchor: { كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون } كما افترض عليكم في مواقيتها.

ELMALILI:2:239/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:239/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:239/r1.claim: Once safe, believers should remember God as taught, fully perform the prayers, and carry out the other rulings they had not known, giving thanks for the instruction.
ELMALILI:2:239/r1.anchor: size o bilmediğiniz ahkâmı ve bu meyanda ahkâm-ı salâtı nasıl tâlim etti ise öylece Allah’ı zikrediniz, namazlarınızı yine kemâliyle kılınız

ELMALILI:2:239/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:239/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:239/r2.claim: Continuing the prayers preserves awareness of this favor; prayer among all religious rulings is analogous to the middle prayer's place among the prayers.
ELMALILI:2:239/r2.anchor: O ahkâm içinde namazlara devam bu fazl ü fazileti unutturmaz. Demek ki namazlar içinde salât-ı vustâ nasılsa bütün ahkâm-ı şer‘iyye içinde namazlar da öyledir.

ELMALILI:2:239/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:239/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:239/r3.claim: The prayer and fear-and-safety reminder is inserted before marriage and divorce rulings have ended; amid discussion of death and divorce, it eloquently urges virtue, prayer, and jihad before the remaining rulings.
ELMALILI:2:239/r3.anchor: Ve bunu anlatmak için nikâh ü talâk mesâili henüz bitmeden arada bilhassa bu emirler verilmiştir. Vefâtın ve talâkın mevzû‘-i bahis olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r2.claim: Prayer is so central and indispensable that it remains obligatory even in frightening danger, though exceptional conditions bring concessions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r2.anchor: Dinin direği, ibadetlerin başı olan namazın, müminin hayatıyla o kadar iç içe, o kadar vazgeçilemez, ihmal edilemez olması istenmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r14.claim: Nisāʾ 4:101–103 teaches congregational prayer when facing an enemy, fighting, or under an imminent attack; this verse addresses individual prayer in broader danger, including war.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r14.anchor: Nisâ sûresinde (101-103) düşmanla karşı karşıya bulunulduğu, fiilen savaşıldığı veya âni bir hücum tehlikesinin bulunduğu zamanlarda

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r15.claim: Prayer must never be abandoned; if circumstances prevent some obligatory or necessary acts, one prays as able, even with some acts omitted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r15.anchor: Çıkan sonuç namazın önemi, terkedilemez oluşu, her hal ve şartta kılınması gerektiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r16.claim: Bodily movements serve prayer’s inner consciousness and relationship with God, so they may be omitted when impossible; remembrance, prayer’s spirit, remains possible in every condition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:238/r16.anchor: Vücut hareketlerini yapmaya bir mani çıktığında bunlar terkedilebilir ancak namaz terkedilemez. Çünkü onun ruhu olan ibadet şuuru (zikir) her durumda mümkündür.

BURHAN:v3p249/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p249/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p249/r1.claim: Putting hearing before knowing conveys warning: hearing is associated with sounds and may seem nearer to a person, although God's knowledge encompasses the manifest and hidden.
BURHAN:v3p249/r1.anchor: تقديم سميع على عليم فإنه يقتضي التخويف والتهديد فبدأ بالسميع لتعلقه بالأصوات

BURHAN:v3p249/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p249/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p249/r2.claim: Forgiveness is safety and mercy is gain, so safety is ranked first; in Sabaʾ the order reverses because mercy covers all creation while forgiveness concerns only some.
BURHAN:v3p249/r2.anchor: فإن المغفرة سلامة والرحمة غنيمة والسلامة مطلوبة قبل الغنيمة وإنما تأخرت في آية سبأ

BURHAN:v3p249/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p249/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p249/r5.claim: Although riding permits prayer more readily than walking, the order puts walkers first as compensation within the concession.
BURHAN:v3p249/r5.anchor: مع أن الراكب متمكن من الصلاة أكثر من الماشي فجبرا له في باب الرخصة

BURHAN:v3p94/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p94/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p94/r4.claim: The lām of purpose may be replaced by bāʾ, min ajl, or kāf; the cited reminder formulas express purpose because of God's sending and teaching.
BURHAN:v3p94/r4.anchor: اللام في المفعول له وتقوم مقامه الباء نحو

AKHFASH:v1p191/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p191/r2.claim: In fear, pray on foot or pray mounted.
AKHFASH:v1p191/r2.anchor: قال {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} يقول: "صلوا رجالا أو صلوا ركبانا"

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r22.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r22.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r22.claim: Rijālan can mean walking on foot; the source groups the verse with the command to come to the pilgrimage walking.
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r22.anchor: " فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا " يعني مشاة نظيرها في سورة الحج " يأتوك رجالا "

DAMGHANI:v1p182/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r6.claim: Dhikr can mean the five daily prayers; Dāmghānī gives another example where trade does not distract men from them.
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r6.anchor: " فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون " يعني الصلوات الخمس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r9.claim: Dhikr can denote the five daily prayers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r9.anchor: فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله ﴾ ، وفي النور :

FARRA:v1p142/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p142/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p142/r4.claim: Farijālan aw rukbānan is accusative because praying on foot or mounted is contingent, not a lasting predicate; both are circumstantial accusatives of the verb ‘pray.’
FARRA:v1p142/r4.anchor: فنصبا لأنهما حالان للفعل لا يصلحان خبرا.

FARRA:v1p142/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p142/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p142/r5.claim: Rijālan here means people on foot (rajāla), paired with riders.
FARRA:v1p142/r5.anchor: إن خفتم أن تصلوا قياما فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا [رجالا يعني: رجالة] فنصبا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r1.claim: The feared danger is an enemy.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r2.claim: Rijālan means on foot; it is the plural of rājil, like qāʾim and qiyām.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r2.anchor: {فرجالا} أي: مشاة؛ جمع راجل. مثل قائم وقيام.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r3.claim: When secure, pray standing; when afraid, pray mounted or walking.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r3.anchor: يقول: تصلي ما أمنت قائما؛ فإذا خفت صليت: راكبا، وماشيا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p92/r4.claim: The fear warranting this concession must be certain, not mere suspicion.

NAHHAS:v1p319/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p319/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p319/r10.claim: The verse is conditional with the answer previously explained; rijālan is circumstantial, meaning pray on foot or mounted if you fear you cannot stand in prayer.
NAHHAS:v1p319/r10.anchor: شرط وجوابه ما قلنا ( فرجالا ) نصب على الحال أي فصلوا رجالا والمعنى فإن خفتم

NAHHAS:v1p319/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p319/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p319/r11.claim: Rājil, rajulān, and rajul can mean one walking; plurals include rajāla, rijāl, rajl, rajla/rajlah, and forms such as rajālī and rajlī.
NAHHAS:v1p319/r11.anchor: ويقال في الجمع رجال مثل كاتب وكتاب ويقال رجل مثل تاجر وتجر

NAHHAS:v1p319/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p319/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p319/r12.claim: An unattributed poetic line, introduced as something a companion said, uses ṣaḥāb as a plural like ṣāḥib/ṣaḥāb.
NAHHAS:v1p319/r12.anchor: كما قال ( وقال صحابي قد شأونك فاطلب ) ويجوز أن يكون رجال جمع رجل

NAHHAS:v1p319/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p319/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p319/r13.claim: Once safe, remember God by standing in prayer, obediently, as previously instructed.
NAHHAS:v1p319/r13.anchor: ( فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله ) أي فقوموا لله قانتين

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r1.claim: Farijālan is a circumstantial accusative with an omitted governor: either “pray walking” or, preferably, “maintain the prayer walking.”
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r1.anchor: منصوب على الحال، والعامل فيه محذوف تقديره: " فصلوا رجالا، أو فحافظوا عليها رجالا وهذا أولى

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r2.claim: Rijāl is a plural of rāʾil/rājil, a person walking on foot without a mount; the cited verse and poetry attest this sense.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r2.anchor: و " رجال " جمع راجل كقائم وقيام، وصاحب وصحاب، يقال منه: رجل يرجل رجلا

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r3.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses rajulān for walking barefoot to the House of God, witnessing the word's on-foot sense.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r3.anchor: علي إذا لاقيت ليلى بخفية أن أزدار بيت الله رجلان حافيا

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r4.speaker: عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r4.claim: Many dialect plurals are listed for the walking person; forms include rajāli, rajāla, rajalān, rajla, arjila, arājil, and arājīl, with readings attributed to ʿIkrima and Ibn Mukhallad and a rare rajjulan.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r4.anchor: وتروى قراءة عن عكرمة، ورجالى ورجالة ورجال وبها قرأ عكرمة وابن مخلد

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r5.claim: The Qurʾanic parallel in 22:27 and another poem use rijālan for going on foot beneath riding animals.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r5.anchor: وقال تعالى: يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر [الحج: 27]

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r6.claim: Rukbān is the plural of rākib; some reserve it for camel riders, calling a horse rider fāris and a donkey or mule rider by the animal's name, though ṣāḥib is better.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r6.anchor: وركبان جمع راكب، قيل: ولا يقال إلا لمن ركب جملا

SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r7.claim: The conjunction aw is variously read as division between cases, permission, or a choice between alternatives.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239/r7.anchor: و " أو " هنا للتقسيم وقيل: للإباحة، وقيل: للتخيير

SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r1.claim: The kāf is accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or a circumstantial of its pronoun; it may instead express cause: remember God because He taught you.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r1.anchor: الكاف في محل نصب: إما نعتا لمصدر محذوف، أو حالا من ضمير المصدر المحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r2.claim: Mā is most naturally a verbal noun; alternatively it is relative, making the command “pray like the prayer He taught you,” with remembrance standing for prayer and the comparison between prayer in danger and safety.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r2.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن تكون مصدرية وهو الظاهر، ويجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي

SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya parses mā lam takūnū as a substitute for the mā in kamā; the Shaykh accepts this but prefers it as substitute for the omitted resumptive pronoun in ʿallamakum, with an Arabic example supporting that ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وعلى هذا التأويل يكون قوله: { ما لم تكونوا } بدلا من " ما " في " كما "

SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r4.claim: The Shaykh prefers taking mā lam takūnū as a substitute for the omitted pronoun in ʿallamakum (allamakumūhu), a construction grammarians permit.
SAMIN-DURR:2:239#2/r4.anchor: وأحسن منه أن يكون " ما لم تكونوا " بدلا من الضمير المحذوف في " علمكم " العائد على الموصول

ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r5.claim: Rijālan is the plural of rājil, following the pattern ṣāḥib/ṣiḥāb.
ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r5.anchor: ورجال جمع راجل ورجال، مثل صاحب وصحاب، أي إن لم يمكنكم

ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r6.claim: When fear prevents a full standing prayer, pray on foot or mounted, still striving to fulfill it as fully as possible.
ZAJJAJ:v1p320/r6.anchor: أي إن لم يمكنكم أن تقوموا قانتين أي عابدين موفين الصلاة حقها

ZAJJAJ:v1p321/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p321/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p321/r1.claim: Once secure, resume standing in devotion and fulfill the obligatory prayer.
ZAJJAJ:v1p321/r1.anchor: أي فإذا أمنتم فقوموا قانتين مؤدين للفرض.

ASAD-NOTES:2:238#n228/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:238#n228/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:238#n228/r1.claim: In any dangerous situation where staying in one place increases peril, obligatory prayer may be performed in any feasible way, even without facing the qiblah.
ASAD-NOTES:2:238#n228/r1.anchor: where remaining for any length of time at one place would only increase the peril: in such an event, the obligatory prayers may be offered

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p939/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p939/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p939/r3.claim: For the people of Paradise, reclining signifies the highest comfort, as though they have nothing else they need to prepare for; Qur’anic reclining is usually linked with food, drink, and family gatherings, with one exception.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p939/r3.anchor: الاتّكاء غاية الراحة كأن الانسان ليس وراءه شيء لأن الانسان لو وراءه شيء لتهيّأ له ولم يتكيء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r1.speaker: الزهري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r1.claim: Al-Zuhrī says that when enemies threaten the Muslims, they may pray facing any direction, on foot or mounted, signaling the prayer in two rakʿas.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r1.anchor: عن الزهري في قوله تعالى ﴿ فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا ﴾ قال إذا أطلت على المسلمين الأعداء فقد حل لهم أن يصلوا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says one rakʿa suffices if the worshipper cannot manage more.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p96#3/r2.anchor: قال قتادة تجزىء ركعة إذا لم يستطيع غيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p542/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p542/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p542/r1.claim: Prayer must still be performed amid family concerns, even in fear on foot or mounted; since this is a harder circumstance, the duty during lesser distractions is even clearer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p542/r1.anchor: فلا بد من أدائها رجالا وركبانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r7.claim: After commanding care for prayers and standing devoutly, the passage addresses the circumstance of fear and grants an allowance to pray walking or riding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r7.anchor: لما ذكر المحافظة على الصلوات، وأمر بالقيام فيها قانتين، كان مما يعرض للمصلين حالة يخافون فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r8.claim: Fear includes an enemy, wild animal, flood, or any other danger; any feared circumstance permits the forms of prayer specified in the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p548/r8.anchor: والخوف يشمل الخوف من: عدو، وسبع، وسيل وغير ذلك، فكل أمر يخاف منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r1.claim: One view reads this as the dawn prayer for a person whose life is threatened in sword combat or similar danger; the verse does not describe the imam-led divided-group form of fear prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r1.anchor: وقالوا: هي صلاة الغداة للذي قد ضايقه الخوف على نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r2.claim: Another explanation takes walkers as a congregational group moving toward the enemy and mounted worshippers as performing prayer by gestures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r2.anchor: وقيل: فرجالا، مشاة بالجماعة لأنهم يمشون إلى العدو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r3.claim: The apparent wording permits prayer while walking; a mounted worshipper gestures and is excused from facing the qibla, according to al-Shāfiʿī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r3.anchor: وظاهر قوله: فرجالا، أنهم يوقعون الصلاة وهم ماشون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r4.speaker: مالك، وأكثر الفقهاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r4.claim: Mālik recommends repeating within the prayer time if someone prayed under a non-enemy fear and then became safe; most jurists treat types of fear alike.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r4.anchor: وقال مالك: يستحب في غير خوف العدو الإعادة في الوقت إن وقع الأمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r5.claim: رجالا is an accusative circumstantial expression with an omitted governing verb; he prefers supplying “maintain the prayers as walkers,” echoing the previous command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r5.anchor: و: رجالا، منصوب على الحال، والعامل محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r6.claim: رجالا is the plural of راجل and means walking on foot without a mount; the verb رجل يرجل describes lacking a ride and walking, with several forms and a Hejazi usage noted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r6.anchor: ورجالا جمع راجل، كقائم وقيام، قال تعالى: وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r7.claim: The cited verse about Banū Ghudāna walking beneath their mounts' bellies uses رجالا for people on foot.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r7.anchor: وبنو غدانة شاخص أبصارهم ... يمشون تحت بطونهن رجالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r8.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r8.claim: The cited verse about visiting God's House on foot uses رجلان to mean walking barefoot.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r8.anchor: علي إذا لا قيت ليلى بخلوة ... أن ازدار بيت الله رجلان حافيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r9.claim: The source lists numerous plural forms for راجل, including رجال, رجيل, رجالى, رجالة, رجلان, رجلة, أرجلة, أراجل, and أراجيل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r9.anchor: قالوا: ويجمع على: رجال ورجيل ورجالى ورجالى ورجالة ورجالى ورجلان ورجلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r10.speaker: عكرمة، وأبو مجلز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r10.claim: ʿIkrima and Abū Mujliz read فرجالا with ḍamma on rāʾ and a doubled jīm; another report from ʿIkrima has the jīm ungeminated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r10.anchor: قرأ عكرمة، وأبو مجلز: فرجالا، بضم الراء وتشديد الجيم، وروي عن عكرمة التخفيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r11.claim: Other reported forms read فرجلا without alif, once with rāʾ ḍamma and doubled jīm and once with rāʾ fatḥa and a still jīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r11.anchor: وقرىء: فرجلا، بضم الراء وفتح الجيم مشدودة بغير ألف وقرىء: فرجلا، بفتح الراء وسكون الجيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r12.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r12.claim: Badīl ibn Maysara reads فَرُجَالًا فَرُكْبَانًا with the conjunction fāʾ repeated; ركبانا is a plural of راكب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r12.anchor: قرأ بديل بن ميسرة: فرجالا فركبانا بالفاء، وهو جمع راكب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r13.speaker: الفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r13.claim: Al-Faḍl says راكب properly denotes a camel rider; a horse rider is فارس, a donkey rider حمار, and a mule rider بغال, though صاحب بغل and صاحب حمار are more eloquent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p549/r13.anchor: قال الفضل: لا يقال راكب إلا لصاحب الجمل، وأما صاحب الفرس فيقال له فارس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r1.claim: Continuing the preceding attribution to Abū Ḥanīfa, the source says prayer while walking or fighting with swords is not permitted unless worshippers can stop and stand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r1.anchor: لا يصلون في حال المشي والمسايفة ما لم يمكن الوقوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r2.claim: The verse sets no number of units for this fearful prayer; most jurists say it is not shortened below the travel-prayer count when the worshippers are on a journey permitting shortening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r2.anchor: ولم تتعرض الآية لعدد الركعات في هذا الخوف، والجمهور أنها لا تقصر الصلاة عن عدد صلاة المسافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r3.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، وغيرهما
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and others say the prayer in this situation is one unit performed by gesture.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة، وغيرهما: تصلى ركعة إيماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the prayer is one unit in combat or otherwise, and if even that is impossible, two takbīrs suffice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك بن مزاحم: تصلى في المسايفة وغيرها ركعة، فإن لم يقدر فليكبر تكبيرتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r5.speaker: إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r5.claim: Isḥāq says one takbīr suffices if that is all the worshipper can manage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r5.anchor: وقال إسحاق: فإن لم يقدر إلا على تكبيرة واحدة أجزأت عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r6.claim: If people mistakenly perceive a dark mass as an enemy, then discover it is not one, Abū Ḥanīfa requires them to repeat the prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r6.anchor: ولو رأوا سوادا فظنوه عدوا ثم تبين أنه ليس بعدو، فقال أبو حنيفة: يعيدون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r7.speaker: مالك، وأحد قولي الشافعي، والمزني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r7.claim: If fear begins after one safe unit, or safety returns after starting in fear, Mālik, one view of al-Shāfiʿī, and al-Muzanī permit completing the prayer on its basis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r7.anchor: فلو صلى ركعة آمنا ثم طرأ له الخوف ركب وبنى، أو عكسه: أتم وبنى، عند مالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa requires restarting if fear arises after opening in safety, but permits building on the prayer if safety returns after it began in fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: إذا استفتح آمنا ثم خاف، استقبل ولم يبن فإن صلى خائفا ثم أمن بنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r9.speaker: أبو يوسف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r9.claim: Abū Yūsuf says the worshipper builds on neither prayer state in either transition between safety and fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r9.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف: لا يبني في شيء من هذا كله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r10.speaker: أكثر العلماء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r10.claim: Prayer's importance is shown by its not being waived even in fear; illness and occupation do not waive it either, and most scholars require a patient unable to perform it to signal with the eyes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r10.anchor: وتدل هذه الآية على عظيم قدر الصلاة وتأكيد طلبها إذا لم تسقط بالخوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r11.claim: Mujāhid explains becoming safe as returning from travel to one's settled home; al-Ṭabarī rejects this, but another comment argues that travel is typically fearful whereas home is secure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد أي: خرجتم من السفر إلى دار الإقامة، ورده الطبري، قيل: ولا ينبغي رده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r12.claim: Another explanation is that the fear which forced the special form of prayer has ceased.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r12.anchor: وقيل: معنى فإذا أمنتم أي: زال خوفكم الذي ألجأكم إلى هذه الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r13.claim: A further explanation takes the phrase to mean whenever you are safe, whether before or after a period of danger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r13.anchor: وقيل: فإذا كنتم آمنين، أي: متى كنتم على أمن قبل أو بعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r14.claim: Remember God by thanking, worshipping, and observing the rites He taught, including how to pray in fear and safety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r14.anchor: فاذكروا الله بالشكر والعبادة كما علمكم أي: أحسن إليكم بتعليمكم ما كنتم جاهليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r15.claim: He parses ما as a verbal noun and the kāf as a simile particle in the first explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r15.anchor: و: ما، مصدرية، و: الكاف، للتشبيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r16.claim: The command calls for remembrance commensurate with the blessing of instruction: worshippers should strive to match the teaching's measure and excellence, even if they cannot equal it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p550/r16.anchor: أمر أن يذكروا الله تعالى ذكرا يعادل ويوازي نعمة ما علمهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r1.claim: “As He taught you” can mean “as He blessed you by teaching you,” naming the effect (teaching) for its cause (divine favor).
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r1.anchor: ومعنى: كما علمكم، كما أنعم عليكم فعلمكم، فعبر بالمسبب عن السبب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r2.claim: The kāf may instead be causal: remember, thank, and worship God because He taught you, since knowledge is the greatest gift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r2.anchor: وقد تكون الكاف للتعليل، أي: فاذكروا الله لأجل تعليمه إياكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r3.claim: ما لم تكونوا تعلمون is the second object of علمكم and stresses that, without God's teaching, people could never have reached this knowledge by their own reason.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r3.anchor: ما لم تكونوا تعلمون ما: مفعول ثان لعلمكم، وفيه الامتنان بالتعليم على العبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r4.speaker: النقاش وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r4.claim: Al-Naqqāsh and others interpret remembrance as performing the taught complete prayer with its conditions and pillars; ما is relative, and the simile contrasts the pre-fear prayer with the safe prayer after fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r4.anchor: وحكى النقاش وغيره أن معنى: فاذكروا الله أي صلوا الصلاة التي قد علمتموها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r5.claim: On that interpretation, Ibn ʿAṭiyya makes ما لم تكونوا a substitute for the ما in كما; otherwise, he says, the wording does not cohere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وعلى هذا التأويل: ما لم تكونوا بدل من: ما، التي في قوله: كما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds a better parsing: it substitutes for the omitted pronoun referring back to ما after علمكم, understood as علمكموه.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r6.anchor: وأحسن منه أن يكون بدلا من الضمير المحذوف في علمكم العائد على ما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r7.claim: Grammarians allow omission of a relative pronoun inside a clause, illustrated by جاءني الذي ضربت أخاك, meaning ضربته أخاك; this licenses his proposed ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p551/r7.anchor: وقد أجاز النحويون: جاءني الذي ضربت أخاك، أي ضربته أخاك، على البدل من الضمير المحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r1.claim: The feared danger may come from an enemy or another source.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r1.anchor: فإن خفتم ) من عدو أو غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r2.claim: Rijālan and rukbānan are circumstantial accusatives describing the implied subject of the conditional response: pray on foot or mounted.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r2.anchor: حالان من الضمير في جواب الشرط أي فصلوا راجلين أو راكبين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r3.claim: Rijāl is the plural of rājil, a person proceeding on foot; some define a rājil more broadly as anyone standing or moving on his feet.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r3.anchor: بمعناه وقيل : الراجل الكائن على رجليه واقفا أو ماشيا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r4.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi infers from the verse's apparent wording that prayer remains obligatory during combat, even without standing.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r4.anchor: واستدل الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه بظاهر الآية على وجوب الصلاة حال المسايفة وإن لم يكن الوقوف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r5.speaker: إمامنا
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r5.claim: The Hanafi Imam holds that walking and fighting invalidate prayer; when forced into that state, one delays prayer and performs it safely afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r5.anchor: وذهب إمامنا إلى أن المشي وكذا القتال يبطلها وإذا أدى الأمر إلى ذلك أخرها ثم صلاها آمنا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi transmits with a sound chain from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri that at the Trench the Prophet missed four prayers until fighting ended, then had Bilal call them and prayed them in their usual form.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r6.anchor: أخرج الشافعي بإسناد صحيح ع أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : حبسنا يوم الخندق حتى ذهب هوى من الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq and other historians say the fear prayer had already been prescribed at Dhat al-Riqaʿ, before the Trench.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r7.anchor: نزلت في ذات الرقاعوهي قبل الخندقكما قاله إبن إسحاق وغيره من أهل السير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r8.claim: A response distinguishes the earlier, less intense fear prayer of 4:102 from the severe-fear procedure in this verse, which was instituted after the Trench.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r8.anchor: لا صلاة شدة الخوف المبينة بهذه الآية والنزاع إنما هو فيهاوهي لم تشرع قبل الخندق بل بعدهوفيه كان الخوف شديدا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r9.speaker: بعض الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r9.claim: Some Hanafis argue that the verse does not explicitly authorize walking or combat during prayer: rājil might mean standing on foot, while total disruption would remove prayer from its form.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r9.anchor: وقد أجاب بعض الحنفية بأنا سلمنا جميع ذلك إلا أن هذه الآية ليست نصا في جواز الصلاة مع المشي أو المسايفة إذ يحتمل أن يكون الراجل فيها بمعنى الواقف على رجليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r10.claim: Al-Alusi concedes that, on fair consideration, the verse's apparent wording clearly supports the Shafiʿi position; religious practice is made easy and the feasible is not abandoned for the impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r10.anchor: ظاهر الآية صريحة مع الشافعية لسبق وقوموا والدين يسر لا عسر والمقامات مختلفة والميسور لا سقط بالمعسور وما لا يدرك لا يترك

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r11.claim: The word is also recited rijālan with a light or doubled rāʾ, and in the singular form rajulan.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r11.anchor: وقريء ( رجالا ) بضم الراء مع التخفيف وبضمها مع التشديد وقريء ( فرجلا ) أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r12.claim: When danger ends, perform the prayer of ordinary safety; Ibn Zayd explains dhikr here as that prayer because it is the prayer's central element.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r12.anchor: أي فصلوا صلاة الأمنكما قال إبن زيدوعبر عنها بالذكر لأنه معظم أركانها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r13.claim: Mujahid interprets safety as leaving travel and returning to a place of residence, apparently as an illustrative case.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r13.anchor: وعن مجاهدإذا خرجتم من دار السفر إلى دار الإقامة ولعله على سبيل التمثيل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r14.claim: Another interpretation takes the command to remember God as gratitude for safety; the suggestion that it requires repeating the prayer is far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r14.anchor: وقيل : المرادأشكروه على الأمنوبعضهم أوجب الإعادة وفسر هذأبأعيدوا الصلاة وهو من البعد بمكان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r15.claim: The comparison means to pray or give thanks as God taught the laws and form of prayer in conditions of safety and fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r15.anchor: أي ذكرا مثل ما ( علمكم ) من الشرائع وكيفية الصلاة حالتيالأمن والخوف أو شكرا يوازي ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r16.claim: Mā may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun, though the relative reading is considered strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r16.anchor: و ( ما ) مصدرية وجوز أن تكون موصولهوفيه بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r17.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r17.claim: Adding takūnū emphasizes the former state of ignorance and makes God's favor clearer, unlike the shorter wording in 96:5.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r17.anchor: وزاد ( تكونوا ) ليفيد النظم ووقع في موضع آخر بدونها كقوله تعالى : ( علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r18.claim: The conditional uses in for possible, relatively rare fear and idhā for expected, frequent safety; the brief first response and expanded second suit their rhetorical settings.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p157/r18.anchor: إيراد الشرطية الأولى بأن المفيد لمشكوكية وقوع الخوف وندرته وتصدير الثانية ب ( إذا ) المنبئة عن تحقق وقوع الأمن وكثرته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r1.claim: Rijālan means walking on foot; rāجل and rijāl follow the pattern ṣāḥib/ṣiḥāb, qāʾim/qiyām, and nāʾim/niyām.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r1.anchor: {فرجالا} أي رجالة يقال: راجل ورجال مثل صاحب وصحاب وقائم وقيام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r2.claim: Rukbānan means riding on mounts and is the plural of rākib.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r2.anchor: {أو ركبانا} على دوابهم وهو جمع راكب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r3.claim: When danger prevents a complete, upright prayer, pray while walking or riding, during combat and sword fighting, facing or not facing the qibla, and gesture for bowing and prostration with the latter lower. The same applies while fleeing a beast or flood that threatens life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r3.anchor: معناه إن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين للصلاة حقها لخوف فصلوا مشاة على أرجلكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r4.claim: This is the prayer for extreme fear; the other forms of fear prayer are treated in Surat al-Nisa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r4.anchor: والصلاة في حال الخوف على أقسام فهذه صلاة شدة الخوف وسائر الأقسام سيأتي بيانها في سورة النساء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r5.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r5.claim: Most scholars say fear does not reduce the number of rakʿas.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r5.anchor: ولا ينتقص عدد الركعات بالخوف عند أكثر أهل العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r6.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Abbas saying that prayer was prescribed as four rakʿas at home, two while traveling, and one in fear; Ata, Tawus, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada likewise say one rakʿa is prayed in intense battle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r6.anchor: روى عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: فرض الله الصلاة على لسان نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحضر أربعا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when combatants are actively striking one another, remembrance with the words “Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest” constitutes their prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إذا كنت في القتال وضرب الناس بعضهم بعضا فقل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r8.claim: Once safe, perform the five prayers in full, with all their proper requirements.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p290/r8.anchor: {فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله} أي فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة بحقوقها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r1.claim: The feared danger may come from an enemy or another source.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r2.claim: In danger, pray on foot or mounted; rijālan is plural of rāجل or rajul in the sense of one walking.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r2.anchor: فصلوا راجلين أو راكبين ورجالا جمع راجل أو رجل بمعناه كقائم وقيام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r3.speaker: الشافعي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that prayer is obligatory even while moving and fighting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r3.anchor: وفيه دليل على وجوب الصلاة حال المسايفة وإليه ذهب الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r4.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says one does not pray while walking and fighting unless able to stop.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى لا يصلى حال المشي والمسايفة ما لم يكن الوقوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r5.claim: This means when the danger has passed and security returns.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r6.claim: Remember God means either perform the ordinary prayer or thank Him for restoring safety.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r6.anchor: صلوا صلاة الأمن أو اشكروه على الأمن

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r7.claim: The remembrance may mirror the laws and prayer taught for both danger and security, or be thanksgiving commensurate with His teaching; mā may be infinitival or relative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r7.anchor: ذكرا مثل ما علمكم من الشرائع وكيفية الصلاة حالتي الخوف والأمن. أو شكرا يوازيه وما مصدرية أو موصولة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:239/r8.claim: The phrase “what you did not know” is the object of “He taught you.”

BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r1.claim: Biqāʿī explains the shift to prayer after the laws of women: family attachments, conflict, and worldly concerns can distract people from prayer and worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r1.anchor: ولما ذكرت أحكام النساء وشعبت حتى ضاق فسيح العقل بانتشارها وكاد أن يضيع في متسع مضمارها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r4.claim: Biqāʿī also summarizes the transition as moving from matters among servants to the relationship between God and them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p449/r4.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه وتعالى ما بين العباد خاصة ذكر ما بينه وبينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r10.claim: Fear may arise in jihad or from an enemy, a wild animal, a creditor one may lawfully flee, or another danger.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r10.anchor: أو نحو ذلك من عدو أو سبع أو غريم يجوز الهرب منه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p453/r11.claim: Rijālan means walking on foot; it is the plural of rājil and comes closest to the ordinary form of prayer.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r1.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r1.claim: Al-Baghawī says that when fear prevents a complete, attentive prayer, one may pray walking on foot; the mounted worshipper prays on an animal as circumstances allow.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r1.anchor: قال البغوي : أي إن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين للصلاة حقها لخوف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r2.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r2.claim: Al-Baghawī explains the mounted prayer as performed on the backs of riding animals in whatever posture is possible.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r2.anchor: أي كائنين على ظهور الدواب على هيئة التمكن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says every rule given in ease is also preserved in hardship, so no state or time removes the blessing of God’s favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r3.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ما من حكم شرعه الله في السعة إلا وأثبته في الضيق والضرورة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r4.claim: The true preservation of prayer is the heart’s complete turning to God; other acts are performed as circumstances permit, otherwise its essence suffices.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r4.anchor: فما اتسع له الحال ما وراء ذلك فعل وإلا اكتفى بحقيقتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r5.claim: In extreme fear, the scholars reduce prayer to one takbīr, which gathers the blessing of four units prayed in ordinary circumstances; its blessing for provision and family remains.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r5.anchor: انتهت الصلاة عند العلماء في شدة الخوف إلى تكبيرة واحدة يجتمع إليها وحدها بركة أربع الركعات التي تقع في السعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī notes that reports describe fourteen or more valid forms of the fear prayer, indicating that its essence has no single fixed outward form.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r6.anchor: وقد وضح باختلاف أحوال صلاة الخوف أن حقيقتها أنها لا صورة لها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r7.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits Ibn ʿUmar’s description of fear prayer: in more intense fear, worshippers pray standing on foot or mounted, facing the qibla or not.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r7.anchor: وروى البخاري في التفسير عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r8.speaker: نافع
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ says Ibn ʿUmar likely attributed the extreme-fear procedure to the Prophet, since it is not the sort of matter based on personal opinion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r8.anchor: قال نافع : لا أرى عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما ذكر ذلك إلا عن رسول الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r9.claim: Amintum means that people have become safe from whatever had frightened them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r9.anchor: أي حصل لكم الأمن مما كان أخافكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r10.claim: Because remembrance and the heart’s ongoing presence are prayer’s chief purpose, invoking God’s supreme name reinforces attention during prayer and other remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r10.anchor: ولما كان المراد الأعظم من الصلاة الذكر وهو دوام حضور القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r11.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r11.claim: Al-Baghawī interprets remembering God here as praying the five obligatory prayers fully and with all their rights.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r11.anchor: قال البغوي : أي فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة بحقوقها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r12.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the verse makes explicit that prayer’s purpose is remembrance, which underlies security in both fear and safety.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r12.anchor: أظهر المقصد في عمل الصلاة وأنه إنما هو الذكر الذي هو قيام الأمن والخوف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r13.claim: Biqāʿī reads the fear concession as preserving actions otherwise barred from prayer, leaving them on their original permissibility in that emergency.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r13.anchor: استثنى الأفعال حال الخوف فأبقيت على الأصل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r14.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Nasāʾī transmit Ibn Masʿūd’s report that the Companions greeted the Prophet during prayer; after his return from Abyssinia he said God had forbidden speaking in prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r14.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : كنا نسلم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r15.claim: Biqāʿī says the Ibn Masʿūd report was judged to refer to the Dhū al-Yadayn event because some routes place his return before the Prophet’s migration to Medina; ʿĀṣim’s report is too weak to outweigh Zayd’s in the Ṣaḥīḥayn.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r15.anchor: لكن عاصم له أوهام في الحديث وإن كان حجة في القراءة فلا يقوى حديثه لمعارضة ما في الصحيحين من حديث زيد الماضي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r16.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r16.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says al-Baqara and al-Nisāʾ were revealed while she was with the Prophet; reports of their marriage and cohabitation place this in the second year after Hijra.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r16.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أنها قالت : ما نزلت سورة البقرة والنساء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r17.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
