BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r17.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī cites Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī’s report that during the Trench battle the Muslims were held from prayer until well into the night after Maghrib.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p455/r17.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : ( حبسنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الخندق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r1.claim: Biqāʿī continues the report attributed on the preceding page to Abū Saʿīd: after the Trench battle delay, Bilāl called the prayer; the Prophet performed Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ thoroughly as usual, before fear prayer was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r1.anchor: فدعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا فأمره فأقام الظهر فصلاها فأحسن صلاتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r2.claim: The two Ṣaḥīḥ collections also report Ibn Masʿūd saying that the Prophet once returned greetings during prayer, but after the Companions returned from the Negus he did not and said prayer is occupied.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r2.anchor: وقد روى الشيخان أيضا حديث ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه بلفظ : كنا نسلم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r3.claim: Biqāʿī notes that the Ibn Masʿūd report does not explicitly prohibit speech, so the earlier possibility remains open.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r3.anchor: لكنه ليس صريحا في تحريم الكلام فيعود الاحتمال السابق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r4.claim: If Zayd’s report is not later than the speech prohibition, the sound conclusion is no distinction between speech and action, since the Dhū al-Yadayn report includes both; al-Shāfiʿī’s wording appears to support this.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r4.anchor: فإن كان الواقع أن حديث زيد متأخر كان ما قلت وإلا كان الذي ينبغي القول به أنه لا فرق بين القول والفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r5.speaker: صاحب التتمة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r5.claim: The Shāfiʿī jurist author of al-Tatimma validated the view that speech and action do not differ in this case.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r5.anchor: كما صححه صاحب التتمة من أصحاب الشافعي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r6.speaker: محيي الدين النواوي والسبكي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r6.claim: Al-Nawawī chose the same view in al-Taḥqīq, and al-Subkī and later scholars followed him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r6.anchor: عن اختيار الشيخ محيي الدين النواوي في كتابه التحقيق وتبعه عليه السبكي وغيره من المتأخرين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r7.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī answered that his critic contradicted both the source and its application, while he himself contradicted neither part of the report.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r7.anchor: وكلام الشافعي ظاهر فيه فإنه قال في الرد على من نسبه إلى أنه خالف في التفريع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r8.claim: Biqāʿī takes kāmā as causal: remember God because He graciously created in you knowledge that rescues you from ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r8.anchor: أي لأجل إنعامه عليكم بأن خلق فيكم العلم المنقذ من الجهل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān allows this causal reading of kāmā and attributes it elsewhere in al-Baḥr to grammarians.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r9.anchor: وقد جوزه أبو حيان في النهر ونقله في موضع آخر منه عن النحاة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r10.claim: What God taught through the Prophet includes the rulings detailed in this sura, along with subtle principles and sciences.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r10.anchor: بما آتاكم على لسان هذا النبي الكريم من الأحكام التي تقدمت في هذه السورة المفصلة ببدائع الأسرار من الأصول ودقائق العلوم كلها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r11.claim: Al-Ḥarālī includes the bodily form of prayer, humility and clearing the soul of intrusive thoughts, reverence in the heart, and deeper secrets reserved for the community’s leading figures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r11.anchor: وقال الحرالي : من أحكام هيئة الصلاة في الأعضاء والبدن وحالها في النفس من الخشوع والإخبات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r12.claim: The preceding discussion of women could suggest that family life consumes time needed for worship, even prompting a wish for monasticism or castration; Biqāʿī says this will be addressed in al-Māʾida.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p457/r12.anchor: وكان هذا السؤال إيماء إلى الاستئذان في الرهبانية والاختصاء الذي سأل فيه من سأل

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that in greater fear one may pray mounted or standing, gesturing to indicate the movements.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: فإذا كان خوف أكثر من ذلك فصلى راكبا أو قائما تومىء إيماء

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r2.claim: The Prophet describes a fear prayer in which two groups alternate one prostration with the imam, while the other guards; if danger is more severe, pray on foot or mounted.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة الخوف أن يكون الإمام يصلي بطائفة معه فيسجدون سجدة واحدة

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r3.claim: The Prophet says the prayer during sword fighting may be one rakʿa in any direction, and it need not be repeated.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة المسايفة ركعة أي وجه كان الرجل يجزىء عنه

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that a mounted person prays on the mount and a walker on foot, as God taught them for the fearful situation.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} قال: يصلي الراكب على دابته والراجل على رجليه

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r5.claim: Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah says that in sword combat a worshipper gestures with the head toward whatever direction he faces.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: إذا كانت المسايفة فليومىء برأسه حيث كان وجهه

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r6.claim: Mujahid says rijālan means walkers and rukbānan refers to the Prophet’s companions on horses; in combat one prays in any direction, standing or mounted, gesturing or speaking as able.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فرجالا} قال: مشاة {أو ركبانا} قال: لأصحاب محمد على الخيل

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r7.claim: Qatada says a frightened person may pray mounted or running, gesturing toward the qibla or another direction.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قال: أحل الله لك إذا كنت خائفا أن تصلي وأنت راكب وأنت تسعى

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r8.claim: Mujahid says in fear of an enemy a rider or walker may gesture in any direction, and one rakʿa suffices.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} قال: هذا في العدو يصلي الراكب والماشي

DURR-FULL:v1p735/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r9.claim: Mujahid gives a graded fallback: pray two rakʿas, then one if unable, then a single takbīr in any direction if even one rakʿa is impossible.
DURR-FULL:v1p735/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: يصلي ركعتين فإن لم يستطع فركعة فإن لم يستطع فتكبيرة

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the fear prayer is one rakʿa at a time.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} قال: ركعة ركعة

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن أنيس
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r2.claim: The Prophet sent ʿAbd Allah ibn Anis to kill Khalid ibn Sufyan; fearing prayer would be delayed, he walked toward him while praying with gestures, then killed him when able.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أنيس قال بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى خالد بن سفيان الهذلي

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r3.claim: Ibrahim says that during pursuit one gestures in whichever direction one faces and makes prostration lower than bowing.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن إبراهيم في قوله {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا}

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r4.claim: Qatada says amid sword combat a rider, walker, or runner prays one rakʿa by gesture in whatever direction faced.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فرجالا أو ركبانا} قال: ذلك عند الضراب بالسيف تصلي ركعة إيماء

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri says the Battle of the Trench kept them from four prayers until the fighting ended; the Prophet ordered an iqāma for each before 2:239 was revealed, and God says He helped the believers at 33:25.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الخندق فشغلنا عن صلاة الظهر والعصر

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r6.claim: Mujahid says becoming safe here means leaving the abode of travel and reaching the abode of settlement.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {فإذا أمنتم} قال: خرجتم من دار السفر إلى دار الإقامه

DURR-FULL:v1p736/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says that once secure, worshippers pray as prescribed; fear had granted them a dispensation.
DURR-FULL:v1p736/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد في الآية قال {فإذا أمنتم} فصلوا الصلاة كما افترض عليكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r1.claim: Muqātil says the fear is fear of the enemy.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a rider prays on the animal and a pedestrian on foot.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس فان خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد ومكحول والحكم والسدي ومالك والأوزاعي والثوري وحسين بن صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r3.claim: These authorities give the same rule and add head gestures toward whatever direction one faces.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r3.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن الحسن ومجاهد ومكحول والحكم والسدى ومالك والاوزاعي والثوري وحسين بن صالح ، نحو ذلك ، وزادوا : يومىء براسه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r4.speaker: عطية العوفي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r4.claim: ʿAṭiyya says in a battle line one prays a rakʿah with two prostrations, gesturing with the head.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r5.claim: Jābir says during sword fighting one gestures with the head in whichever direction one faces.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r5.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله ، قال : اذا كانت المسايفة فليومىء براسه حيث كان وجهه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r6.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعطية والحكم وحماد وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r6.claim: These authorities are reported to share Jābir's rule for prayer during sword fighting.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r6.anchor: وروى عن الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعطية والحكم وحماد وقتادة نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk allows two rakʿahs during fighting in any direction, gesturing if unable to bow or prostrate.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r8.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي والزهري ومكحول والربيع بن أنس وسفيان الثوري والحسن بن صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r8.claim: These authorities are reported to hold that this prayer is two rakʿahs.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r8.anchor: وروى عن إبراهيم النخعي والزهري 1 ومكحول والربيع بن انس وسفيان الثوري

IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r9.claim: Muqātil explains becoming safe as becoming safe from the enemy.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p450/r9.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، قوله : فاذا امنتم من العدو

IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r1.claim: Mujāhid says safety means leaving the abode of travel for the abode of residence.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قوله : فاذا امنتم قال : الخروج من دار السفر الى دار المقام

IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r2.claim: Muqātil explains remembering God as praying as He taught you.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان فاذكروا الله كما علمكم يقول : صلوا كما علمكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God taught people to pray on a mount when riding and on foot when walking.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p451/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس فاذا امنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون يعني : كما علمكم ان يصلي الراكب على دابته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r1.claim: When safety returns, remembering God means resuming the familiar prescribed prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r1.anchor: أراد الصلاة أي ارجعوا إلى الذكر المعروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r2.claim: Using if for fear but when for safety promises Muslims that victory and security will come.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r2.anchor: وجاء في الأمن بإذا وفي الخوف بإن بشارة للمسلمين بأنهم سيكون لهم النصر والأمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r3.claim: The comparison asks for remembrance like God's gift of teaching detailed sacred law, understood as gratitude and recompense; its causal sense arises from the comparison, and some call it a causal kāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p470/r3.anchor: الكاف للتشبيه أي اذكروه ذكرا يشابه ما من به عليكم من علم الشريعة في تفاصيل هذه الآيات المتقدمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r1.claim: The normal prayer posture is standing in qunut, meaning solemnity, tranquility, and stillness of the limbs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى بالقيام له في الصلاة بحالة قنوت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r2.claim: In danger one may pray walking or mounted, using gestures and head motions in whatever direction one faces.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r2.anchor: فرخص لعبيده في الصلاة رجالا متصرفين على الأقدام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r3.claim: Any danger to life permits the concession; the congregational fear prayer with divided groups is not addressed here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r3.anchor: فكل أمر يخاف منه على روحه فهو مبيح ما تضمنته هذه الآية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r4.claim: Threats include combat, a pursuing beast or enemy, or a flood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r4.anchor: في حال المسايفة أو من سبع يطلبه أو عدو يتبعه أو سيل يحمله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r5.claim: Malik recommends repeating within the prayer time if safety returns after fear of a beast or similar danger, distinguishing it from a fighting enemy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r5.anchor: وفرق مالك رحمه الله بين خوف العدو المقاتل وبين خوف السبع ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r6.speaker: أكثر فقهاء الأمصار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r6.claim: Most jurists treat fear of an enemy and other life-threatening dangers alike.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r6.anchor: وأكثر فقهاء الأمصار على أن الأمر سواء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r7.claim: Rijālan is a plural of rā jil or rajul, deriving from walking on foot without a mount.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى فرجالا هو جمع راجل أو رجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya lists plural forms of the foot-walker noun, including rijāl and arājīl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r8.anchor: ويجمع على رجال ورجيلى ورجالى ورجالى ورجالة ورجال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r9.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi cites a line using rajulān for walking to the House of God without shoes.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r10.claim: In 22:27 rijālan means arriving on foot without mounts, whereas rijāl in 2:282 is the ordinary collective noun for men.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r10.anchor: فهذه الآية وقوله تعالى: يأتوك رجالا [الحج: 27] هما من لفظ الرجلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة وأبو مجلز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r11.claim: Ikrima and Abu Majliz read rijālan with a damma on rā and doubled, open jim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r11.anchor: وحكى المهدوي عن عكرمة وأبي مجلز أنهما قرآ «فرجالا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r12.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r12.claim: A second reading attributed to Ikrima has a damma on rā and an ungeminated jim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r12.anchor: وعن عكرمة أيضا أنه قرأ «فرجالا» بضم الراء وتخفيف الجيم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r13.claim: Al-Tabari transmits a reading without alif, farajulan, on the fu'l pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r13.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن بعضهم أنه قرأ «فرجلا» دون ألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r14.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r14.claim: The majority of readers recite aw rukbānan.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r15.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r15.claim: Buda y l ibn Maysara reads the sequence with fa before rukbānan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p324#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة «فرجالا فركبانا» بالفاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r1.claim: The concession lets one face any direction and move as needed to save oneself; rukbān is the plural of rākib.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r1.anchor: وهذه الرخصة في ضمنها بإجماع من العلماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r2.speaker: مالك وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r2.claim: Malik and a group do not reduce prayer units for fear; a traveler still prays two units.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r2.anchor: فمالك رحمه الله وجماعة من العلماء لا يرون أن ينقص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r3.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r3.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, and others hold that a person in fear prays one unit with gestures.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: يصلي ركعة إيماء.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r4.claim: Mujahid transmits Ibn Abbas's statement that prayer is four units at home, two while traveling, and one in fear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r4.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عباس أنه قال: «فرض الله الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r5.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says someone fearing death in combat prays one unit, or two takbīrs if unable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك بن مزاحم: «يصلي صاحب خوف الموت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r6.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r6.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir cites Ishaq ibn Rahwayh as holding that one takbīr suffices if that is all the person can manage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r6.anchor: وقال إسحاق بن راهويه: «فإن لم يقدر إلا على تكبيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r7.claim: One group reads this as thanking God after danger passes for teaching a valid prayer that prevents a missed prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r7.anchor: فقالت فرقة: المعنى فإذا زال خوفكم الذي ألجأكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r8.claim: Another group says that whenever secure, before or after danger, people should perform the complete prayer God taught.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المعنى فإذا كنتم آمنين قبل أو بعد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r9.claim: On the second interpretation, mā lam takūnū is appositive to mā in kamā; on the first, it is the object of allamakum.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r9.anchor: وقوله على هذا التأويل ما لم تكونوا بدل من «ما»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r10.claim: Mujahid interprets becoming safe as leaving travel for residence; al-Tabari rejects this and Ibn Atiyya finds it strained.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r11.claim: On the thanksgiving reading, kāf compares human remembrance with God's favor of teaching the prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r11.anchor: والكاف في قوله كما للتشبيه بين ذكر الإنسان لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r12.claim: If remember means pray, kāf compares the servant's prayer with the form God taught.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p325/r12.anchor: ومن تأول «اذكروا» بمعنى صلوا على ما ذكرناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r1.claim: If you fear an enemy, pray on foot: rijāl is the plural of rājil, and rukbān is the plural of rākib.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r1.anchor: أي خفتم عدوا فصلوا رجالا وهو جمع راجل والركبان جمع راكب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r2.claim: The command to pray in every circumstance demonstrates the emphatic importance of prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على تأكيد أمر الصلاة لأنه أمر بفعلها على كل حال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r3.claim: This verse is said to have come after the fear-prayer instructions in 4:102 and to cover even more severe danger, such as sword fighting, when one prays as able.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r3.anchor: وقيل إن هذه الآية انزلت بعد التي في سورة النساء لإن الله تعالى وصف لهم صلاة الخوف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet prayed Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ after the twilight had disappeared on the day of the Trench.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r4.anchor: ما روى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه صلى يوم الخندق الظهر والعصر والمغرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد، أبو بكر الأثرم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the Trench incident preceded this verse's revelation; al-Athram says the verse shows that the delayed prayers on that day were superseded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p284#2/r5.anchor: أن أبا سعيد روى أن ذلك كان قبل نزول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r4.claim: After commanding preservation of prayer and its limits, God addresses combat as a circumstance that prevents performing prayer in its fullest form.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r4.anchor: ذكر الحال التي يشتغل الشخص فيها عن أدائها على الوجه الأكمل، وهي حال القتال والتحام الحرب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r5.claim: In severe danger, pray in any condition, on foot or mounted, whether facing the qibla or turned away from it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r5.anchor: أي: فصلوا على أي حال كان، رجالا أو ركبانا: يعني: مستقبلي القبلة وغير مستقبليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r6.speaker: مالك ونافع وابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r6.claim: Malik transmits from Nafi that Ibn Umar described the severe-fear prayer as on foot or mounted, facing or away from the qibla; Nafi thought Ibn Umar derived this from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r6.anchor: قال نافع: لا أرى ابن عمر ذكر ذلك إلا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r7.claim: Ibn Umar also reports that under still greater fear a worshipper may pray mounted or standing, signaling the movements.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r7.anchor: ولمسلم أيضا عن ابن عمر قال: فإن كان خوف أشد من ذلك فصل راكبا أو قائما تومئ إيماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن أنيس الجهني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r8.claim: Sent by the Prophet to kill Khalid ibn Sufyan al-Hudhali near Arafah, Abdullah ibn Unays feared missing Asr and prayed by gestures while facing him; Ahmad and Abu Dawud transmit the report with a good chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r8.anchor: وفي حديث عبد الله بن أنيس الجهني لما بعثه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، إلى خالد بن سفيان الهذلي ليقتله وكان نحو عرفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r9.claim: This is one of God's concessions to His servants, by which He removes burdens and constraints from them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p655/r9.anchor: وهذا من رخص الله التي رخص لعباده ووضعه الآصار والأغلال عنهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that a rider prays on the animal and a pedestrian prays on foot.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال في هذه الآية: يصلي الراكب على دابته والراجل على رجليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد ومكحول والسدي والحكم ومالك والأوزاعي والثوري والحسن بن صالح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r2.claim: These authorities give the same ruling and add that the worshipper signals with the head, facing whichever direction is possible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r2.anchor: وروي عن الحسن ومجاهد ومكحول والسدي والحكم ومالك والأوزاعي والثوري والحسن بن صالح نحو ذلك وزادوا: يومئ برأسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r3.claim: Jabir says that in sword combat one should signal with the head toward whichever direction one faces; he connects this practice to the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r3.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: إذا كانت المسايفة فليومئ برأسه [إيماء] (7) حيث كان وجهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r4.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعطية والحكم وحماد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir reports that these authorities also hold the same head-gesture ruling for the fear prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r4.anchor: وروي عن الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعطية والحكم وحماد وقتادة نحو ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r5.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r5.claim: Ahmad holds that in some cases, when the two armies are fully engaged, the fear prayer may be performed as one rak'a.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب الإمام أحمد فيما نص عليه، إلى أن صلاة الخوف تفعل في بعض الأحيان ركعة واحدة إذا تلاحم الجيشان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r6.claim: The Prophet taught that obligatory prayer is four rak'as at home, two while traveling, and one in fear; Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others share the one-rak'a view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: فرض الله الصلاة على لسان نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحضر أربعا، وفي السفر ركعتين وفي الخوف ركعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري وقتادة والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r7.claim: Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others affirm that the fear prayer in this situation is one rak'a.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r7.anchor: وبه قال الحسن البصري وقتادة والضحاك وغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r8.speaker: الحكم وحماد وقتادة والثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r8.claim: When Ibn Jarir asked al-Hakam, Hammad, and Qatada about sword combat, they answered that the prayer is one rak'a; al-Thawri transmits the same view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r8.anchor: سألت الحكم وحمادا وقتادة عن صلاة المسايفة، فقالوا: ركعة وهكذا روى الثوري عنهم سواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r9.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r9.claim: Ibn Jarir selects the view that the fear prayer in the reported case is one rak'a, citing Jabir's report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: صلاة الخوف. ركعة واختار هذا القول ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r10.speaker: الأوزاعي ومكحول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r10.claim: Al-Awza'i says that if a siege leaves no chance to pray, worshippers gesture individually; if even that is impossible, they delay until safe, then pray two rak'as, or one if necessary, and defer altogether if no movement is possible. Makhul agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r10.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: إن كان تهيأ الفتح، ولم يقدروا على الصلاة صلوا إيماء كل امرئ لنفسه فإن لم يقدروا على الإيماء أخروا الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r11.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r11.claim: At the siege of Tustar, Anas and Abu Musa could not pray during intense fighting, so they prayed after sunrise when the battle ended; Anas said he would not trade that prayer for the world.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r11.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: حضرت مناهضة حصن تستر عند إضاءة الفجر، واشتد اشتعال القتال فلم يقدروا على الصلاة فلم نصل إلا بعد ارتفاع النهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r12.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r12.claim: Al-Bukhari frames the issue under a chapter on praying while besieging fortresses and meeting the enemy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p656/r12.anchor: باب الصلاة عند مناهضة الحصون ولقاء العدو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r1.speaker: الصحابة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r1.claim: At Khandaq the Prophet delayed Asr until sunset because of fighting; later, when ordering the march to Banu Qurayza, some prayed on the way while others waited until sunset there, and he censured neither group.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r1.anchor: حديث تأخيره، عليه السلام، صلاة العصر يوم الخندق بعذر المحاربة إلى (2) غيبوبة الشمس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r2.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Khandaq and Banu Qurayza episodes show al-Bukhari's preference that prayer can be delayed when fighting prevents it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على اختيار البخاري لهذا القول والجمهور على خلافه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r3.claim: The majority disagrees, arguing that the Quranic and hadith forms of the fear prayer were not legislated at Khandaq but only afterward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r3.anchor: ويعولون على أن صلاة الخوف على الصفة التي ورد بها القرآن في سورة النساء ووردت (4) بها الأحاديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r4.speaker: مكحول والأوزاعي والبخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r4.claim: Makhul, al-Awza'i, and al-Bukhari answer that later legislation of formal fear prayer does not bar a special, rare case of delaying prayer, citing the Companions' public, unchallenged practice at Tustar under Umar.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657/r4.anchor: بأن مشروعية صلاة الخوف بعد ذلك لا تنافي جواز ذلك؛ لأن هذا حال نادر خاص فيجوز فيه مثل ما قلنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.claim: When safe, worshippers should perform prayer as commanded and complete its bowing, prostration, standing, sitting, humility, and other elements.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.anchor: أي: أقيموا صلاتكم كما أمرتم فأتموا (5) ركوعها وسجودها وقيامها وقعودها وخشوعها وهجودها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.claim: God has favored people, guided them to faith, and taught what benefits them in this life and the next; they should respond with gratitude and remembrance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.anchor: مثل ما أنعم عليكم وهداكم للإيمان وعلمكم ما ينفعكم في الدنيا والآخرة، فقابلوه بالشكر والذكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir links the command to resume full prayer after fear with the rule that once secure believers establish prayer at its appointed times.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.anchor: كقوله بعد ذكر صلاة الخوف: {فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا} [النساء:103]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir directs readers to the later account of fear-prayer forms under the verse about the Prophet leading prayer in battle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.anchor: عند قوله تعالى: {وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة} الآية [النساء:102]

JISHUMI:v1p884#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p884#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p884#2/r11.claim: ‘On foot or riding’ is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, with an omitted verb meaning ‘pray.’
JISHUMI:v1p884#2/r11.anchor: وأما (رجالا) فتقديره: فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا

JISHUMI:v2p961/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r1.claim: Fear is the opposite of security.

JISHUMI:v2p961/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r2.claim: Rijāl is the plural of rājil, on the pattern of tājir/tujjār and other listed singular-plural pairs.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r2.anchor: والرجال جمع راجل، نحو تاجر وتجار وقائم وقيام

JISHUMI:v2p961/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r3.claim: Riding is mounting or being on something; rākib has the plural rukbān, like fāris/fursān.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r3.anchor: والركوب: العلو على الشيء يقال: راكب وركبان جمع راكب

JISHUMI:v2p961/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r4.claim: ‘On foot or riding’ and the following phrase are accusative circumstantial expressions with an omitted governing verb, ‘pray.’
JISHUMI:v2p961/r4.anchor: نصبا على الحال، والعامل فيه محذوف، وتقديره: فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا

JISHUMI:v2p961/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r5.claim: After commanding observance of prayer, God permits prayer in the presence of an enemy when fear prevents its full conditions and due performance.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r5.anchor: الرخصة حال العدو في الصلاة لما تقدم الأمر بالمحافظة عليها

JISHUMI:v2p961/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r6.claim: The phrase is explained as praying while walking on foot or riding on the backs of animals.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r6.anchor: قيل: مشاة على أرجلكم أو ركبانا على ظهور دوابكم

JISHUMI:v2p961/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r7.claim: A second gloss says to pray on foot or on the backs of animals, identifying this as the prayer of fear.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r7.anchor: وقيل: على أرجلكم أو ظهور دوابكم، وهو صلاة الخوف

JISHUMI:v2p961/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p961/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan permits the prayer of fear to consist of one rakʿa.

JISHUMI:v2p961/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r9.speaker: أهل العراق
JISHUMI:v2p961/r9.claim: The Iraqi jurists say fear does not change the number of rakʿas: two while travelling and four while resident; Jishumi prefers this because one rakʿa is not a prayer and dawn prayer is not shortened.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r9.anchor: فأما أهل العراق فقالوا: لا يؤثر الخوف في عدد الركعات، ففي السفر ركعتان، وفي الحضر أربع

JISHUMI:v2p961/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r10.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p961/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, like al-Shāfiʿī, allows prayer by gestures while walking or fighting, facing whatever direction one is going.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r10.anchor: قال الحسن: يجوز، وهو قول الشافعي

JISHUMI:v2p961/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
JISHUMI:v2p961/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions do not allow prayer by gestures while walking and fighting.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r11.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: لا يجوز

JISHUMI:v2p961/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r12.claim: When fear ends, the worshipper returns to the secure state of prayer.

JISHUMI:v2p961/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r13.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد والأصم
JISHUMI:v2p961/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, and al-Aṣamm understand remembering God as performing the complete prayer of a secure person, with all its pillars.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r13.anchor: قيل: صلوا صلاة الآمن بتمام أركانها (كما علمكم)، عن الحسن وابن زيد والأصم

JISHUMI:v2p961/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p961/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p961/r14.claim: Another explanation takes the command as praising and extolling God for teaching people what they did not know of their religion.
JISHUMI:v2p961/r14.anchor: اذكروا الله بالحمد له والثناء عليه كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون من أمور دينكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r1.claim: “When you are secure” means when your fear has passed.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r2.claim: Remember God as He taught you what you did not know about prayer in conditions of safety.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r3.claim: Alternatively, thank God for security and worshipfully remember His kindness in teaching the laws and how to pray in fear and safety.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p317/r3.anchor: فإذا أمنتم فاشكروا الله على الأمن واذكروه بالعبادة كما أحسن اليكم بما علمكم من الشرائع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r24.claim: Rijal is the plural of rajil, a person on foot, and rukban the plural of rakib, a rider, like qa'im and qiyam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r24.anchor: الرجال جمع راجل , والركبان جمع راكب , مثل قائم وقيام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r25.claim: When afraid of an enemy, pray on foot or mounted, facing the qibla or away from it, standing or walking, as ability permits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r25.anchor: يعني فإن خفتم من عدوكم , فصلوا على أرجلكم أو ركائبكم , وقوفا ومشاة , إلى القبلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r26.claim: The majority require two units even in fearful prayer, while al-Hasan says a fearful person prays one unit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r26.anchor: فذهب الجمهور إلى أنها على عددها تصلى ركعتين , وقال الحسن : تصلى ركعة واحدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r27.speaker: أهل الحجاز
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r27.claim: The people of the Hijaz hold that the prayer need not be repeated after safety returns because the worshipper had an excuse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r27.anchor: فذهب أهل الحجاز إلى سقوط الإعادة عنه لعذره

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r28.speaker: أهل العراق
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r28.claim: The people of Iraq require repetition after safety because walking during prayer is an act outside the prayer itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r28.anchor: وذهب أهل العراق إلى وجوب الإعادة عليه لأن مشيه فيها عمل ليس منها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r29.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r29.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the command after safety as praying in the manner God taught.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r29.anchor: معناه فإذا أمنتم فصلوا كما علمكم , وهو قول ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r30.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r30.claim: Another interpretation is to remember God with praise and thanks for teaching the religion and what people did not know.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p307/r30.anchor: فاذكروه بالثناء عليه والحمد له , كما علمكم من أمر دينكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

MUJAHID:v1p111/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p111/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
MUJAHID:v1p111/r1.claim: Ibrahim says this applies during pursuit in battle: a rider or person on foot prays two units wherever facing, indicating with the head.
MUJAHID:v1p111/r1.anchor: عن مغيرة عن إبراهيم في قوله ﴿ فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا ﴾ قال هذا عند المطاردة في القتال يصلي ركعتين الراكب والراجل حيث كان وجهه يومئ برأسه إيماء

MUJAHID:v1p111/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p111/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p111/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses rijālan as walking on foot.
MUJAHID:v1p111/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ فرجالا ﴾ يعني مشاة

MUQATIL:2:238-239/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:238-239/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:238-239/r4.claim: In intense fear, pray two units on foot or mounted facing any possible direction; if unable to prostrate, nod with the head, make prostration lower than bowing, and place the forehead on nothing.
MUQATIL:2:238-239/r4.anchor: يقول: على أرجلكم أو على دوابكم، فصلوا ركعتين

MUQATIL:2:238-239/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:238-239/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:238-239/r5.claim: Once safe, remember God by praying, as He taught what people did not previously know.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.claim: If fear comes from an enemy or another cause, the worshipper prays while walking.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.anchor: فإن كان بكم خوف من عدو أو غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.claim: Rijālan is a circumstantial accusative meaning on foot; it is the plural of rājil, like qāʾim/qiyām.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.anchor: حال أى فصلوا راجلين وهو جمع راجل كقائم وقيام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.claim: The fearful may pray mounted, with gestures; facing the qibla is waived.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.anchor: وحدانا بإيماء ويسقط عنه التوجه إلى القبلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.claim: Security means the fear has ended.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.claim: When safe, remember God by performing the normal prayer of security.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.claim: Remember God in the way He taught you, including the ordinary prayer you had not known before His instruction.

BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r1.claim: Fear means fear of an enemy or another danger; رجالاً is an accusative circumstantial plural of راجل, with an omitted verb understood as 'pray walking'; ركبانا means mounted riders.
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r1.anchor: منصوب على الحال وعامله محذوف تقديره فصلوا راجلين

BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that one must stop if possible: prayer while walking and fighting is not performed until stopping becomes possible, when one prays standing.
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r2.anchor: ومذهب أبي حنيفة أنهم لا يصلون في حال المشي والمسايفة

BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r3.claim: When danger is gone, 'remember God' means perform the normal prayer, whose most important pillar is remembrance.
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r3.anchor: وزال خوفكم {فاذكروا الله} أي : فصلوا صلاة الأمن

BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r4.claim: The comparison means prayer should accord with God's teaching about its form; alternatively, give thanks in proportion to His teaching of previously unknown laws, including prayer in fear and safety.
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r4.anchor: والمراد بالتشبيه أن تكون الصلاة المؤداة موافقة لما علمه الله

BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r5.claim: Prayer is a banquet prepared for monotheists five times each day; its varied pillars and actions are like dishes, each bringing pleasure and atonement for sins.
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أن الصلاة بمنزلة الضيافة قد هيأها الله للموحدين

BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār relates God's words to Moses: noon prayer brings forgiveness, heavier scales, angelic intercession, and heaven's opening; for afternoon, requests are granted; sunset opens heaven; night prayer is better than the world and leaves worshippers like newborns.
BURSEVI:v1p305#2/r6.anchor: وعن كعب الأحبار أنه قال : قال الله لموسى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r1.claim: The phrase “if you fear” refers to fear that is alarm or panic.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r2.claim: Farijālan means pray on foot; a person is called rajil or rājil when walking because he has no mount, and the passage lists several Arabic singular and plural forms.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r3.claim: The phrase aw rukbānan is coordinated with farijālan; rajil and rājil are forms for a person walking, with multiple plural forms cited from al-Tabari and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r3.anchor: رجل الإنسان يرجل رجلا إذا عدم المركوب ومشى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r4.claim: After commanding prayer with calm, stillness, and composure in the usual safe condition, God addresses occasional danger and makes clear that prayer never falls away; He permits prayer on foot or mounted, with gestures of the head, in any direction.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r5.claim: This concession covers an isolated worshipper whose life is endangered by combat, a pursuing beast or enemy, a flood, or any other imminent threat to life.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r5.anchor: وهذه هي صلاة الفذ الذي قد ضايقه الخوف على نفسه في حال المسايفة أو من سبع يطلبه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r6.claim: Scholars agree that in this danger concession a person may face whichever direction and move or turn as needed to save himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r6.anchor: هذه الرخصة في ضمنها إجماع العلماء أن يكون الإنسان حيثما توجه من السموت ويتقلب ويتصرف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi limits this prayer to serious enemy danger: the forces see each other and Muslims are exposed to weapons, or a reliable messenger reports an enemy approaching rapidly; otherwise the concession does not apply.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r7.anchor: فقال الشافعي: هو إطلال العدو عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r8.claim: If Muslims pray the danger prayer on reliable news that the enemy is near and the enemy then leaves, Abu Hanifa says they must repeat it; another opinion says no repetition is due.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r9.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r9.claim: Abu Umar distinguishes the severe-danger prayer here, which may be on foot or mounted and with or without facing the qibla, from the congregational prayer of fear led by an imam, whose rules are treated in Surat al-Nisaʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r9.anchor: قال أبو عمر: فالحال التي يجوز منها للخائف أن يصلي راجلا أو راكبا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r10.claim: Malik distinguishes fear of a fighting enemy from threats such as a beast or flood; if nonenemy danger passes, he recommends repeating the prayer within its time, while most jurists treat the cases alike.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r10.anchor: وفرق مالك بين خوف العدو المقاتل وبين خوف السبع ونحوه من جمل صائل أو سيل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r11.claim: Abu Hanifa says fighting invalidates prayer; al-Qurtubi says the Ibn Umar report contradicts him and the verse’s plain sense is stronger evidence against him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239/r11.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: إن القتال يفسد الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi infers that permitting some prayer conditions to be omitted shows that fighting during prayer does not invalidate it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r1.anchor: قال الشافعي: لما رخص تبارك وتعالى في جواز ترك بعض الشروط دل ذلك على أن القتال في الصلاة لا يفسدها،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r2.speaker: مالك والشافعي وجماعة من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r2.claim: Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and other scholars hold that fear prayer has no fewer rakʿas than the traveler’s prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r2.anchor: عند مالك والشافعي وجماعة من العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r3.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, and others say the worshipper prays one rakʿa by gesture during fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما:: يصلي ركعة إيماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that prayer was prescribed as four rakʿas at home, two when traveling, and one in fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r4.anchor: روى مسلم عن بكير بن الأخنس عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: فرض الله الصلاة على لسان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r5.speaker: ابن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says Bukayr alone transmitted the one-rakʿa report and is not authoritative when isolated; two rakʿas in fear and travel avoids disagreement with certainty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: انفرد به بكير بن الأخنس وليس بحجة فيما ينفرد به، والصلاة أولى ما احتيط فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says someone fearing death in sword combat or similar prays one rakʿa, or two takbirs if unable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك بن مزاحم: يصلي صاحب خوف الموت في المسايفة وغيرها ركعة فإن لم يقدر فليكبر تكبيرتين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r7.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r7.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh says that if the person can manage only one takbir, it suffices; Ibn al-Mundhir cites him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r7.anchor: وقال إسحاق بن راهويه: فإن لم يقدر إلا على تكبيرة واحدة أجزأت عنه ذكره ابن المنذر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r8.claim: When safe, worshippers return to the commanded prayer with its complete pillars.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: { فإذآ أمنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم } أي ارجعوا إلى ما أمرتم به من إتمام الأركان.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r9.claim: Mujahid interprets safety as leaving the land of travel for the land of residence; al-Tabari rejects this interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «أمنتم» خرجتم من دار السفر إلى دار الإقامة ورد الطبري على هذا القول.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r10.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r10.claim: A group interprets safety as the end of the fear that compelled this form of prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة: «أمنتم» زال خوفكم الذي ألجأكم إلى هذه الصلاة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r11.claim: Malik allows building on the prayer when one rakʿa was prayed safely before fear forced the worshipper to mount, or when a fearful rider becomes safe and dismounts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r11.anchor: فقال مالك: إن صلى ركعة آمنا ثم خاف ركب وبنى، وكذلك إن صلى ركعة راكبا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r12.speaker: الشافعي والمزني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r12.claim: This is also one of al-Shafiʿi’s opinions and the view of al-Muzani.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r12.anchor: وهو أحد قولي الشافعي، وبه قال المزني.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r13.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r13.claim: Abu Hanifa requires restarting if safety changes to fear after the prayer begins, but allows building if fear changes to safety.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r13.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: إذا افتتح الصلاة آمنا ثم خاف استقبل ولم يبن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r14.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r14.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says a worshipper who is on foot may build on the prayer after the change of state, but a rider may not.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r14.anchor: وقال الشافعي: يبني النازل ولا يبني الراكب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r15.speaker: أبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r15.claim: Abu Yusuf says building on the prayer is not allowed in any of these cases.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r15.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف: لا يبني في شيء من هذا كله.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r16.claim: One explanation takes remembrance as gratitude for being taught a prayer that fulfills the obligation without missing any prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r16.anchor: قيل: معناه اشكروه على هذه النعمة في تعليمكم هذه الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r17.claim: The kāf in “as” carries the sense of gratitude or requital, as in doing for someone what they did for you.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r17.anchor: فالكاف في قوله «كما» بمعنى الشكر تقول: افعل بي كما فعلت بك كذا مكافأة وشكرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r18.claim: In “what you did not know,” mā is the object of “He taught you.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r18.anchor: و «ما» في قوله «ما لم» مفعولة ب «علمكم».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r19.claim: Prayer’s root sense is supplication, and fear is especially a time for supplication; therefore fear cannot cancel prayer, a fortiori illness and other states cannot.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r19.anchor: الصلاة أصلها الدعاء، وحالة الخوف أولى بالدعاء فلهذا لم تسقط الصلاة بالخوف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r20.claim: God requires preserving prayer in health or illness, residence or travel, ability or incapacity, fear or safety; its obligation is never impaired.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r20.anchor: فأمر الله سبحانه وتعالى بالمحافظة على الصلوات في كل حال من صحة أو مرض، وحضر أو سفر،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r21.claim: The commentary says the rules for a sick person’s prayer will be discussed at the end of Ali Imran.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r21.anchor: وسيأتي بيان حكم المريض في آخر «آل عمران» إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r22.claim: Prayer must be performed however possible, even by eye gesture; unlike other worship, it never falls away through excuses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r22.anchor: حتى لو لم يتفق فعلها إلا بالإشارة بالعين لزم فعلها، وبهذا تميزت عن سائر العبادات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r23.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r23.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says scholars deem abandoning prayer punishable by death because it resembles faith and is a pillar that cannot be delegated by body or wealth, like the two testimonies.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r23.anchor: قال ابن العربي: ولهذا قال علماؤنا: وهي مسألة عظمى، إن تارك الصلاة يقتل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r24.claim: The author defers the scholars’ discussion of the legal status of one who abandons prayer to the commentary on Bara'a.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:239#2/r24.anchor: وسيأتي ما للعلماء في تارك الصلاة في «براءة» إن شاء الله تعالى.

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r1.claim: After requiring preservation of prayer with its pillars and conditions, God limits that full observance to times of safety rather than fear.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r1.anchor: هذه المحافظة على هذا الحد لا تجب إلا مع الأمن دون الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r2.claim: The phrase is also transmitted with rāʾ vowelled ḍamma, with a doubled rāʾ, or in the singular form rajulā.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r2.anchor: بضم الراء و { رجالا } بالتشديد و { رجلا }

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r3.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī takes the fear to be fear of an enemy, with the object of the verb omitted because context makes it understood.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r3.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله معنى الآية : فإن خفتم عدوا فحذف المفعول لإحاطة العلم به

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf allows fear of an enemy or any other cause; al-Rāzī prefers this because the concession applies whenever fear occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r4.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : فإن كان بكم خوف من عدو أو غيره ، وهذا القول أصح

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r5.speaker: قول ثالث
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r5.claim: A third interpretation is fear that prayer time will expire if prayer is delayed until the fighting ends.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r5.anchor: وفيه قول ثالث وهو أن المعنى : فإن خفتم فوات الوقت إن أخرتم الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r6.claim: On the time-expiration reading, the verse underscores the obligation to pray within its prescribed time, permitting concessions to preserve it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r6.anchor: الآية تدل على تأكيد فرض الوقت حتى يترخص لأجل المحافظة عليه بترك القيام

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r7.claim: Rijālan is the plural of rājil, someone on foot, whether walking or standing still; the source lists several plural forms.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r7.anchor: رجالا جمع راجل مثل تجار وتاجر وصحاب وصاحب والراجل هو الكائن على رجله ماشيا كان أو وافقا

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r8.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r8.claim: Al-Qaffāl allows rijāl to be a plural of a plural, deriving it through the plural forms of rājil.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r8.anchor: ما ذكره القفال ، وهو أنه يجوز أن يكون جمع الجمع ، لأن راجلا يجمع على راجل

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r9.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r9.claim: Rukbān is the plural of rākib; al-Qaffāl says rākib is used for someone on a camel, while a person on a horse is called fāris.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r9.anchor: والركبان جمع راكب ، مثل فرسان وفارس ، قال القفال : ويقال إنه إنما يقال راكب لمن كان على جمل

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r10.claim: Rijālan is an accusative circumstantial expression whose governing verb is omitted; the implied wording is “pray on foot or riding.”
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r10.anchor: رجالا نصب على الحال ، والعامل فيه محذوف ، والتقدير : فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا

RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r11.claim: Fear prayer has two settings: during fighting, addressed here, and outside fighting, addressed in the prayer-of-fear passage in al-Nisāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131/r11.anchor: صلاة الخوف قسمان أحدهما : أن تكون في حال القتال وهو المراد بهذه الآية والثاني : في غير حال القتال

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits prayer in joined battle on foot or mounted, facing or away from the qibla, with gestures for bowing and prostration, making the latter lower and avoiding needless shouts.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r1.anchor: فمذهب الشافعي رحمه الله أنهم يصلون ركبانا على دوابهم ومشاة على أقدامهم

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says a person on foot does not pray in this situation but delays the prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : لا يصلي الماشي بل يؤخر

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر ونافع
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar understands the phrase to permit facing or not facing the qibla; Nāfiʿ says he believes Ibn ʿUmar received this from the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عمر : { فرجالا أو ركبانا }

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that severe fear makes it impossible to keep facing the qibla or safely stand for full bowing and prostration, so the wording permits turning away and gesturing.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r4.anchor: لا يمكن معه المحافظة على الاستقبال

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.claim: Prayer still requires intention and recitation; extraneous speech and unnecessary cries remain forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r5.anchor: فعل القلب وهو النية ، وذلك لا يسقط لأنه لا يتبدل حال الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.claim: Standing and sitting fall away, while gestures replace bowing and prostration; the gesture for prostration should be lower than the one for bowing.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r6.anchor: وأما الركوع والسجود فالإيماء قائم مقامهما

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.claim: Purification does not lapse because water or earth can be used; al-Rāzī prefers allowing tayammum with dust while mounted when water is present but unsafe to use, since danger to life outweighs fear of thirst.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r7.anchor: وأما ترك الطهارة فغير جائز لأجل الخوف ، فإنه يمكنه التطهير بالماء أو التراب

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī cites the Prophetic instruction to perform of a commanded act whatever one is able to do as the basis for the Shāfiʿī position.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r8.anchor: إذا أمرتكم بشيء فأتوا منه ما استطعتم

RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that the Prophet delayed prayer on the day of the Trench, so Muslims should do likewise.
RAZI-FULL:v6p131#2/r9.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة بأنه عليه السلام أخر الصلاة يوم الخندق

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that the danger at the Trench did not reach the severity described here, so this verse abrogated the Prophet's earlier delay.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r1.anchor: لم يبلغ الخوف هذا الحد ومع ذلك فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أخرى الصلاة فعلمنا كون هذه الآية ناسخة لذلك الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r2.claim: Fear prayer applies in battle and outside it; battle may be obligatory, permitted, or prohibited. Fighting unbelievers is the original case, and fighting rebels is included by the command in 49:9.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r2.anchor: أما القتال الواجب فهو كالقتال مع الكفار وهو الأصل في صلاة الخوف ، وفيه نزلت الآية

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو المحاسن الطبري
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū al-Maḥāsin al-Ṭabarī says defending oneself is permitted rather than obligatory, except when an unbeliever targets the person, when defense is obligatory to protect Islam's rights.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو المحاسن الطبري في كتاب شرح المختصر : أن دفع الإنسان عن نفسه مباح غير واجب

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r4.claim: Fear prayer is permitted when defending oneself or any animal whose life is protected.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r4.anchor: أما القتال في الدفع عن النفس وفي الدفع عن كل حيوان محترم ، فإنه يجوز فيه صلاة الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r5.claim: Jurists differ over defending property: al-Rāzī prefers permitting fear prayer, reasoning from the report that one killed defending property is a martyr, which equates its defense with self-defense.

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r6.claim: The opposing view denies the property-defense concession, reasoning that the sanctity of another protected interest is greater.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r6.anchor: والثاني : لا يجوز لأن حرمة الزوج أعظم

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r7.claim: The concession does not apply to prohibited fighting: it would assist wrongdoing, and a sinful aggressor does not merit such assistance.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r7.anchor: أما القتال المحظور فإنه لا تجوز فيه صلاة الخوف ، لأن هذا رخصة والرخصة إعانة

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r8.claim: Outside battle, the concession applies to someone fleeing fire, flood, or a predatory animal, and to an insolvent debtor fearing detention who cannot prove insolvency, because the wording is general.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r8.anchor: أما الخوف الحاصل لا في القتال ، كالهارب من الحرق والغرق والسبع وكذا المطالب بالدين إذا كان معسرا

RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r9.claim: Although the wording may suggest battle, the verse establishes the concession to prevent harm, and that rationale also applies to noncombat dangers.
RAZI-FULL:v6p132/r9.anchor: إلا أنه لما ثبت هناك دفعا للضرر ، وهذا المعنى قائم ههنا ، فوجب أن يكون ذلك الحكم مشروعا

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that prayer was prescribed as four rakʿas at home, two while traveling, and one during fear.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : فرض الله على لسان نبيكم الصلاة في الحضر أربعا

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r2.claim: The majority require four rakʿas at home and two on a journey whether or not there is fear; they regard Ibn ʿAbbās's view as abandoned.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r2.anchor: والجمهور على أن الواجب في الحضر أربع ، وفي السفر ركعتان سواء كان في الخوف أو لم يكن

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r3.claim: When the fear that occasioned the concession ends, “remember God” means perform prayer as taught and prescribed; the ordinary duty returns, and prayer is called remembrance in 62:9.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r3.anchor: فاذكروا بمعنى فافعلوا الصلاة كما علمكم

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r4.speaker: قول ثان
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r4.claim: A second interpretation takes remembrance of God to mean thanking Him for granting safety.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r4.anchor: أي فاشكروه لأجل إنعامه عليكم بالأمن

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that this conditional remembrance should be specific to safety; gratitude is due during fear as well, since both conditions contain God's blessings and the fear comes from unbelievers, not God.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r5.anchor: طعن القاضي في هذا القول وقال : إن هذا الذكر لما كان معلقا بشرط مخصوص

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r6.speaker: قول ثالث
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r6.claim: A third interpretation includes both prayer and gratitude, with gratitude specifically due upon safety and performed alongside prayer at its appointed times.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r6.anchor: القول الثالث : أنه دخل تحت قوله

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r7.claim: “As He taught you” recalls God's favor in teaching and guiding people; without His guidance they would not have reached this knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r7.anchor: فبيان إنعامه علينا بالتعليم والتعريف ، وأن ذلك من نعمه تعالى ، ولولا هدايته لم نصل إلى ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r8.speaker: أصحابنا والمعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī's Ashʿarite colleagues explain the teaching as God creating knowledge, while the Muʿtazila explain it as furnishing proofs and acts of grace.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r8.anchor: ثم إن إصحابنا فسروا هذا التعليم بخلق العلم والمعتزلة فسروه بوضع الدلائل ، وفعل الألطاف

RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r9.claim: What people did not know points to the era before Muḥammad's mission, a time of ignorance and error.
RAZI-FULL:v6p133/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى ما قبل بعثة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من زمان الجهالة
